title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
authors: Julius Adebayo, Justin Gilmer, Michael Muelly, Ian Goodfellow, Moritz Hardt, Been Kim
relevance: Shows some saliency methods are insensitive to model/data randomization, motivating the whole reliability/robustness-of-explanations line that the attacks exploit.

title: Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning For Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Robin Sommer, Vern Paxson
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
relevance: The seminal statement of why ML NIDS underperforms operationally - traffic diversity, the closed-world assumption, and the semantic gap - framing every later drift/generalization study.

title: RISE: Randomized Input Sampling for Explanation of Black-box Models
authors: Vitali Petsiuk, Abir Das et al.
relevance: Introduced the deletion and insertion AUC metrics that most later faithfulness evaluations (including NIDS ones) reuse as automatic, human-free measures of attribution quality.

title: Testing Intrusion Detection Systems: A Critique of the 1998 and 1999 DARPA Intrusion Detection System Evaluations as Performed by Lincoln Laboratory
authors: John McHugh
venue: ACM Transactions on Information and System Security (TISSEC)
relevance: The original benchmark-dataset critique: methodological flaws in the DARPA/KDD lineage (synthetic traffic realism, attack taxonomy, scoring) that still propagate into every KDD99/NSL-KDD-based traffic-classification result.

title: Evaluating the Visualization of What a Deep Neural Network Has Learned
authors: Wojciech Samek, Alexander Binder et al.
relevance: Origin of the AOPC (area over the perturbation curve) metric: quantifies heatmap quality by flipping most-relevant inputs first; the direct ancestor of the deletion-style metrics later applied to traffic classifiers.

title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post hoc Explanation Methods
authors: Dylan Slack, Sophie Hilgard, Emily Jia, Sameer Singh, Himabindu Lakkaraju
venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES)
relevance: The seminal 'scaffolding' attack showing perturbation-based explainers LIME and SHAP can be reliably fooled to hide a biased classifier; the reference attack for all explanation-manipulation work in security.

title: Deep packet: a novel approach for encrypted traffic classification using deep learning
authors: Mohammad Lotfollahi, Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Ramin Shirali Hossein Zade, Mohammdsadegh Saberian
input_representation: first 1500 raw IP-packet bytes (masked MAC/IP), 1D vector
relevance: Deep Packet: stacked autoencoder + 1D-CNN over the first 1500 raw packet bytes (identifying header fields masked to avoid bias) for app identification and traffic characterization on ISCX; the single most-cited raw-byte model that XAI studies explain.

title: Interpretation of Neural Networks is Fragile
authors: Amirata Ghorbani, Abubakar Abid, James Zou
relevance: Shows imperceptible input perturbations can drastically change saliency/feature-importance while keeping the prediction; Hessian-geometry analysis argues fragility may be fundamental to gradient explanations.

title: Malware traffic classification using convolutional neural network for representation learning
authors: Wei Wang, Ming Zhu, Xuewen Zeng, Xiaozhou Ye, Yiqiang Sheng
input_representation: raw session bytes rendered as 28x28 grayscale image
relevance: First representation-learning traffic classifier: raw session bytes are rendered as a grayscale image and fed to a 2D-CNN (introduced USTC-TFC2016); saliency on these byte-images is the archetypal explanation target.

title: Towards Faithfully Interpretable NLP Systems: How Should We Define and Evaluate Faithfulness?
authors: Alon Jacovi, Yoav Goldberg
relevance: Position paper separating faithfulness from plausibility and arguing faithfulness should be graded, not binary; supplies the conceptual vocabulary any evaluation section needs.

title: A Benchmark for Interpretability Methods in Deep Neural Networks (ROAR)
authors: Sara Hooker, Dumitru Erhan, Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Been Kim
relevance: RemOve And Retrain: retraining after feature removal avoids the OOD confound; found many popular attribution methods are no better than random, a key caution for scoring traffic-feature attributions.

title: ERASER: A Benchmark to Evaluate Rationalized NLP Models
authors: Jay DeYoung, Sarthak Jain et al.
relevance: Defines comprehensiveness and sufficiency (with AOPC-binned variants), the faithfulness metric pair most frequently ported from NLP into tabular and security settings.

title: End-to-end encrypted traffic classification with one-dimensional convolution neural networks
authors: Wei Wang, Ming Zhu, Jinlin Wang, Xuewen Zeng, Zhongzhen Yang
input_representation: first 784 raw bytes of a session/flow (1D vector)
relevance: Canonical 1D-CNN on the first 784 raw bytes of a session, end-to-end on ISCX VPN-nonVPN; the default raw-byte baseline nearly every XAI-for-traffic paper explains or attacks.

title: The (Un)reliability of Saliency Methods
authors: Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Sara Hooker et al.
relevance: Shows a meaningless constant input shift changes many attribution methods' outputs (input invariance), an early demonstration that both methods and naive evaluations are unreliable; relevant to preprocessing-heavy traffic features.

title: On the Robustness of Interpretability Methods
authors: David Alvarez-Melis, Tommi S. Jaakkola
relevance: Introduces local Lipschitz robustness metrics for explanations and shows current methods score poorly; one of the standard stability metrics in Quantus and in security evaluations.

title: An Analysis of the 1999 DARPA/Lincoln Laboratory Evaluation Data for Network Anomaly Detection
authors: Matthew V. Mahoney, Philip K. Chan
relevance: Classic demonstration of simulation artifacts: anomaly detectors on DARPA'99 keyed on idiosyncratic TTL values, client addresses and other regularities absent in real traffic - the archetype of the spurious-correlation findings now rediscovered in CIC datasets.

title: On the (In)fidelity and Sensitivity for Explanations
authors: Chih-Kuan Yeh, Cheng-Yu Hsieh et al.
relevance: Defines the infidelity and max-sensitivity metrics (implemented in Captum/Quantus) and shows the degenerate optimum of pure sensitivity (a constant explanation), i.e. single metrics can be trivially satisfied.

title: ET-BERT: A Contextualized Datagram Representation with Pre-training Transformers for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Xinjie Lin, Gang Xiong, Gaopeng Gou, Zhen Li, Junzheng Shi, Jing Yu
relevance: The dominant 12-layer/12-head traffic BERT. Verified from full text: its 'Interpretability' section (4.4) contains only a cipher-randomness analysis (performance attributed to 'the imperfect randomness of the ciphers of encrypted payloads') and t-SNE of representations -- attention weights are never analyzed or validated as explanations.

title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time
authors: Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Roberto Jordaney, Johannes Kinder, Lorenzo Cavallaro
relevance: Shows published malware-classifier results are inflated by spatial and temporal bias (training on future data), introduces time-aware evaluation constraints and the AUT metric that temporal-degradation studies now use as standard.

title: Mobile Encrypted Traffic Classification Using Deep Learning: Experimental Evaluation, Lessons Learned, and Challenges
authors: Giuseppe Aceto, Domenico Ciuonzo, Antonio Montieri, Antonio Pescape
input_representation: systematic comparison: payload bytes vs. protocol-field time series inputs
relevance: The reference experimental evaluation of SAE/CNN/LSTM mobile traffic classifiers across input designs (payload bytes vs. header-field series), explicitly cataloguing dataset/input pitfalls - groundwork every explanation study cites.

title: FS-Net: A Flow Sequence Network For Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Chang Liu, Longtao He, Gang Xiong, Zigang Cao, Zhen Li
input_representation: packet-length sequence of a flow (no payload)
relevance: FS-Net: multi-layer bi-GRU encoder-decoder with reconstruction loss over raw packet-length sequences only; the canonical sequence-model baseline whose explanations live in packet-size/timing space rather than byte space.

title: Evaluating Explainable AI: Which Algorithmic Explanations Help Users Predict Model Behavior?
authors: Peter Hase, Mohit Bansal
relevance: The controlled human simulatability protocol; shows subjective user ratings do not predict measured utility, motivating objective metrics while bounding what automatic metrics can claim.

title: FlowPrint: Semi-Supervised Mobile-App Fingerprinting on Encrypted Network Traffic
authors: Thijs van Ede, Riccardo Bortolameotti, Andrea Continella, Jaehyun Hwang, Andreas Peter, et al.
relevance: Open-world app fingerprinting without prior app knowledge: builds fingerprints from destination correlations and detects previously UNSEEN apps at 93.5% precision, a core open-world capability prior classifiers lacked.

title: Robust Network Traffic Classification
authors: Jun Zhang, Xiao Chen, Yang Xiang, Wanlei Zhou, Jie Wu
relevance: Seminal zero-day traffic work: combines supervised and unsupervised learning (RTC) to identify traffic of applications never seen in training while retaining accuracy on known classes.

title: LEMNA: Explaining Deep Learning based Security Applications
authors: Wenbo Guo, Dongliang Mu, Jun Xu, Purui Su, Gang Wang, Xinyu Xing
relevance: Security-specific local explanation method (fused-lasso + mixture regression) built because LIME/SHAP assumptions fail on security models (RNNs, feature dependency); the standard baseline that later human/runtime evaluations (e.g., Warnecke) test.

title: Lucid: A Practical, Lightweight Deep Learning Solution for DDoS Attack Detection
authors: R. Doriguzzi-Corin, S. Millar, S. Scott-Hayward, J. Martinez-del-Rincon, D. Siracusa
input_representation: per-flow matrix of 11 packet-level attributes x n packets (packet-feature sequence)
relevance: LUCID: lightweight CNN over a flow matrix of 11 per-packet attributes for DDoS detection with 40x faster inference; its authors also published a companion activation-analysis, making it a standard explainability testbed for attack detection.

title: Accurate Decentralized Application Identification via Encrypted Traffic Analysis Using Graph Neural Networks (GraphDApp)
authors: Meng Shen, Jinpeng Zhang, Liehuang Zhu, Ke Xu, Xiaojiang Du
input_representation: Traffic Interaction Graph (TIG) built from packet sizes/directions of bidirectional bursts
relevance: GraphDApp converts a flow's bidirectional packet-size interactions into a Traffic Interaction Graph classified by a GNN for DApp fingerprinting (1,300 DApps); graph inputs invite subgraph-style (GNNExplainer-like) explanations, unlike byte saliency.

title: Quantus: An Explainable AI Toolkit for Responsible Evaluation of Neural Network Explanations and Beyond
authors: Anna Hedstrom, Leander Weber, Dilyara Bareeva, Daniel Krakowczyk, Franz Motzkus, Wojciech Samek, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Marina M.-C. Hohne
relevance: The reference open-source library implementing 30+ evaluation metrics across faithfulness, robustness, localisation, complexity, randomisation and axiomatic categories; the practical tool for running metric batteries on traffic classifiers.

title: The Disagreement Problem in Explainable Machine Learning: A Practitioner's Perspective
authors: Satyapriya Krishna, Tessa Han, Alex Gu, Steven Wu, Shahin Jabbari, Himabindu Lakkaraju
relevance: Formalizes and empirically documents how often post-hoc explainers disagree (top-k features, signs, ranks) and shows practitioners resolve disagreement ad hoc; the anchor citation for the disagreement problem.

title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: M. Wang, K. Zheng, Y. Yang, X. Wang
explanation_method: SHAP (local + global), comparing one-vs-all vs multiclass classifiers
relevance: First systematic SHAP-for-IDS paper and the most-cited applied work in this sub-literature; template for hundreds of follow-ups.

title: A Diagnostic Study of Explainability Techniques for Text Classification
authors: Pepa Atanasova, Jakob Grue Simonsen et al.
relevance: Defines a battery of diagnostic properties (agreement with human rationales, faithfulness, confidence indication, rationale consistency) and shows no explainer dominates across datasets and models.

title: MIMETIC: Mobile encrypted traffic classification using multimodal deep learning
authors: Giuseppe Aceto, Domenico Ciuonzo, Antonio Montieri, Antonio Pescape
input_representation: multimodal: first payload bytes + per-packet protocol-field sequence (dir/size/TCP win/IAT)
relevance: MIMETIC fuses two modalities - raw payload bytes and packet-level protocol-field sequences - with intra/inter-modality learning for mobile app classification; multimodal inputs mean explanations must attribute across heterogeneous views.

title: CADE: Detecting and Explaining Concept Drift Samples for Security Applications
authors: Limin Yang, Wenbo Guo, Qingying Hao, Arridhana Ciptadi, Ali Ahmadzadeh, Xinyu Xing, Gang Wang
relevance: Contrastive-learning latent space plus distance-to-class-centroid explanations for drifting samples; authors argue explaining 'distance' beats explaining a 'decision boundary' for drift -- an alternative explanation target evaluated on network intrusion and malware data.
_key: t:cade detecting and explaining concept drift samples for security applications

title: An Explainable Deep Learning-enabled Intrusion Detection Framework in IoT Networks
authors: M. Keshk, N. Koroniotis, N. Pham, N. Moustafa, B. Turnbull, A. Y. Zomaya
explanation_method: SPIP framework: SHAP + Permutation Feature Importance + Individual Conditional Expectation + Partial Dependence Plots over an LSTM
relevance: Multi-technique global+local explanation stack over the three most common NIDS datasets; frequently cited applied framework.

title: Datanet: Deep Learning Based Encrypted Network Traffic Classification in SDN Home Gateway
authors: Pan Wang, Feng Ye, Xuejiao Chen, Yi Qian
input_representation: raw packet bytes (per-packet vectors)
relevance: Datanet trains MLP, stacked-autoencoder, and CNN classifiers on raw packet bytes of ISCX VPN-nonVPN for app-aware SDN home-gateway control; a canonical multi-architecture raw-byte baseline.

title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Metrics
authors: Richard Tomsett et al.
relevance: Meta-evaluates fidelity metrics themselves via reliability statistics and finds they are statistically unreliable and mutually inconsistent; direct evidence that the metrics, not just the methods, are suspect.

title: OpenXAI: Towards a Transparent Evaluation of Model Explanations
authors: Chirag Agarwal, Dan Ley et al.
relevance: Open benchmark with 22 metrics (faithfulness, stability, fairness) over tabular datasets plus a synthetic generator with ground truth; the plug-and-play harness closest to tabular flow-feature NIDS evaluation.

title: Debugging Tests for Model Explanations
authors: Julius Adebayo, Michael Muelly et al.
relevance: Evaluates explanations by whether they help detect injected data/model/test-time bugs, an end-task-grounded alternative to perturbation metrics that maps well onto NIDS shortcut-learning audits.

title: Troubleshooting an Intrusion Detection Dataset: the CICIDS2017 Case Study
authors: Gints Engelen, Vera Rimmer, Wouter Joosen
relevance: Documents label errors, CICFlowMeter implementation bugs (wrong TCP session termination, duplicated flows) and attack-simulation flaws in CIC-IDS2017, showing benchmark results on the uncorrected dataset are unreliable.

title: FlowPic: A Generic Representation for Encrypted Traffic Classification and Applications Identification
authors: Tal Shapira, Yuval Shavitt
input_representation: 2D histogram image of packet sizes vs. arrival times per flow window
relevance: FlowPic turns a flow into a 2D packet-size/arrival-time histogram image classified by a LeNet-style CNN (VPN and Tor categories); pixel-saliency explanations map back to size-time bins, making it a favorite XAI subject.

title: New Directions in Automated Traffic Analysis (nPrint / nPrintML)
authors: Jordan Holland, Paul Schmitt, Nick Feamster, Prateek Mittal
input_representation: nPrint: constant-size bit-aligned binary packet representation (every header bit a feature, -1 padding)
relevance: nPrint defines a standard bit-level packet representation consumed by AutoML (nPrintML); because each input bit maps to a named protocol header bit, feature-importance explanations are directly semantically interpretable - the paper itself does such model analysis.

title: Yet Another Traffic Classifier: A Masked Autoencoder Based Traffic Transformer with Multi-Level Flow Representation (YaTC)
authors: Ruijie Zhao, Mingwei Zhan, Xianwen Deng, Yanhao Wang, Yijun Wang, Guan Gui, Zhi Xue
relevance: MAE-pretrained ViT over an MFR byte matrix with packet-level and flow-level attention modules. Verified from full text: zero interpretability content -- attention is ablated only for accuracy/complexity (ISCXVPN2016, ISCXTor2016, USTC-TFC2016, CICIoT2022); no attention map is ever shown or validated.

title: TSCRNN: A novel classification scheme of encrypted traffic based on flow spatiotemporal features for efficient management of IIoT
authors: Kunda Lin, Xiaolong Xu, Honghao Gao
input_representation: raw byte segments of flows: CNN spatial features + stacked BiLSTM temporal features
relevance: TSCRNN extracts spatial features from raw flow bytes with CNN then temporal dependencies with stacked BiLSTM for IIoT encrypted traffic; a widely-cited CNN+RNN hybrid baseline in later XAI comparisons.

title: Do Feature Attribution Methods Correctly Attribute Features?
authors: Yilun Zhou, Serena Booth et al.
relevance: Dataset-modification procedure yielding ground-truth attributions; finds saliency, occlusion, LIME and SHAP all deviate substantially from ground truth in controlled semi-natural settings.

title: PERT: Payload Encoding Representation from Transformer for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Hong Ye He, Zhi Guo Yang, Xiang Ning Chen
input_representation: payload bytes tokenized as words for BERT-style dynamic word embedding
relevance: PERT is the first BERT-style pre-training applied to encrypted traffic: payload bytes are tokenized and contextually embedded, then fine-tuned for classification; starts the pre-trained-transformer line whose attention maps XAI work probes.

title: TFE-GNN: A Temporal Fusion Encoder Using Graph Neural Networks for Fine-grained Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Haozhen Zhang, Le Yu, Xi Xiao, Qing Li, Francesco Mercaldo, Xiapu Luo, Qixu Liu
input_representation: byte-level graphs per packet (bytes as nodes, PMI co-occurrence edges), separate header/payload graphs
relevance: TFE-GNN encodes each packet's raw bytes as a point-wise-mutual-information graph, embeds header and payload graphs with dual GNNs and cross-gated fusion, then fuses temporally; the canonical byte-graph model, where explanations become node/edge importance over bytes.

title: GEE: A Gradient-based Explainable Variational Autoencoder for Network Anomaly Detection
authors: Q. P. Nguyen, K. W. Lim, D. M. Divakaran, K. H. Low, M. C. Chan
explanation_method: Gradient fingerprinting on VAE reconstruction (per-feature gradient of anomaly score)
relevance: Early and much-cited gradient-based explanation for unsupervised flow anomaly detection; gradient fingerprints double as attack signatures.

title: Benchmarking Attribution Methods with Relative Feature Importance (BIM)
authors: Mengjiao Yang, Been Kim
relevance: Constructs semi-synthetic datasets with known relative feature importance to give attribution evaluation a controlled ground truth; a template for building ground-truth traffic datasets.

title: A Consistent and Efficient Evaluation Strategy for Attribution Methods (ROAD)
authors: Yao Rong, Tobias Leemann et al.
relevance: Shows perturbation evaluation strategies leak class information through the mask shape (explaining conflicting rankings) and proposes noisy-linear imputation (ROAD) to fix it without retraining.

title: INSOMNIA: Towards Concept-Drift Robustness in Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Giuseppina Andresini, Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Corrado Loglisci, Annalisa Appice, Lorenzo Cavallaro
relevance: First major drift-mitigation framework for NIDS proper: semi-supervised incremental adaptation with nearest-centroid label estimation, and uses explainability-based feature-importance analysis to interpret how the model evolves under drift.

title: Transcending TRANSCEND: Revisiting Malware Classification in the Presence of Concept Drift
authors: Federico Barbero, Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Lorenzo Cavallaro
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
relevance: Formalizes and extends Transcend's conformal rejection (TRANSCENDENT), showing classification-with-rejection generalizes across malware domains and classifiers as a principled defense against drifting inputs.

title: On Quantitative Aspects of Model Interpretability
authors: An-phi Nguyen, Maria Rodriguez Martinez
relevance: Decomposes interpretability evaluation into fidelity, simplicity and other objectively measurable aspects with concrete metrics; scaffolding for a metrics-taxonomy chapter.

title: Robust Network Intrusion Detection Through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)
authors: P. Barnard, N. Marchetti, L. A. DaSilva
explanation_method: SHAP explanations of XGBoost, then an autoencoder TRAINED ON THE EXPLANATIONS to flag unseen attacks
relevance: Uses explanations as features for o.o.d./novel-attack detection - a reusable pattern (explanation-space monitoring) for traffic classifiers.

title: Evaluating Explanation Methods for Deep Learning in Security
authors: Alexander Warnecke, Daniel Arp, Christian Wressnegger, Konrad Rieck
relevance: THE template for explanation evaluation in security: defines descriptive accuracy, sparsity, stability, efficiency, robustness and completeness for malware/NIDS models and finds IG and LRP comply best; image-style assumptions break on structured security data.

title: Which Explanation Should I Choose? A Function Approximation Perspective to Characterizing Post Hoc Explanations
authors: Tessa Han, Suraj Srinivas et al.
relevance: Explains WHY methods disagree: each explainer is a local function approximation under a different neighborhood/loss, so no method is universally faithful and disagreement is structural, not a bug.

title: The Effectiveness of Feature Attribution Methods and Its Correlation with Automatic Evaluation Scores
authors: Giang Nguyen, Daeyoung Kim et al.
relevance: Large human study finding automatic attribution metrics correlate poorly with actual human-AI team performance; a core citation for 'metrics may not measure what we care about'.

title: DeepAID: Interpreting and Improving Deep Learning-based Anomaly Detection in Security Applications
authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, Ying Zhong, Su Wang, Han Zhang, Jiahai Yang, Xingang Shi, Xia Yin
relevance: Reference-based interpretation dedicated to UNSUPERVISED security anomaly detectors (contrast anomaly vs. a normal reference) plus a Distiller extension turning interpretations into a rule-like updatable model -- a non-attribution explanation form applied to network anomaly detection (Kitsune etc.).

title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (Trustee)
authors: Arthur S. Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta, Lisandro Z. Granville
relevance: Extracts high-fidelity, low-complexity, stable decision-tree surrogates from any black-box network-security ML model to expose shortcut learning, o.o.d. blind spots and spurious correlations -- the flagship decision-tree-surrogate work for network models.

title: HuntGPT: Integrating Machine Learning-Based Anomaly Detection and Explainable AI with Large Language Models (LLMs)
authors: T. Ali, P. Kostakos
explanation_method: SHAP + LIME attributions rendered into analyst-facing narratives by GPT-3.5 in a dashboard
relevance: First widely-known XAI+LLM analyst interface for network anomaly detection; starts the LLM-explanation wave.

title: Explaining Anomalies Detected by Autoencoders Using Shapley Additive Explanations
authors: L. Antwarg, R. M. Miller, B. Shapira, L. Rokach
explanation_method: KernelSHAP adapted to autoencoder reconstruction error (contributing vs offsetting features per anomaly)
dataset: Tabular/UCI + applicable to any AE-based detector; heavily reused by network-anomaly papers
relevance: The standard recipe for applying SHAP to unsupervised autoencoder detectors - the technique most network-anomaly XAI papers copy.

title: E-XAI: Evaluating Black-Box Explainable AI Frameworks for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Osvaldo Arreche, Tanish R. Guntur, Jack W. Roberts, Mustafa Abdallah
relevance: End-to-end framework grading SHAP and LIME on NIDS models with six metrics (descriptive accuracy, sparsity, stability, efficiency, robustness, completeness) over NSL-KDD, CICIDS-2017 and RoEduNet-SIMARGL2021; the closest existing template to XAI-for-traffic-classification evaluation.

title: Explaining Network Intrusion Detection System Using Explainable AI Framework
authors: Shraddha Mane, Dattaraj Rao
relevance: Early NIDS-XAI pipeline layering SHAP, LIME, Contrastive Explanations, ProtoDash and Boolean rules over a DNN on NSL-KDD; representative of the analyst-facing-in-name-only genre that later human studies interrogate.

title: The Cross-evaluation of Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese, Luca Pajola, Mauro Conti
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
relevance: First formal model (XeNIDS) for cross-dataset evaluation of ML-NIDS, exposing why papers that reuse the same outdated datasets as isolated testbeds overstate reliability and hide generalization failures.

title: Evaluating Local Explanation Methods on Ground Truth
authors: Riccardo Guidotti
relevance: Uses synthetic and transparent-model ground truth to score LIME/SHAP-style explainers on tabular and text data; the closest general template for ground-truth evaluation on flow-feature classifiers.

title: Anomaly Detection in the Open World: Normality Shift Detection, Explanation, and Adaptation (OWAD)
authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, Kai Wang, Rui Yu, Su Wang, Han Zhang, Zhihua Wang, Minghui Jin, Jiahai Yang, Xingang Shi, Xia Yin
relevance: Detects, EXPLAINS, and adapts to normality shift (benign-side drift) in DL anomaly detection unsupervised, reducing labeling overhead and validated on long-term NIDS/log data plus a SCADA deployment - the detect-explain-adapt loop for the benign class.

title: NetMamba: Efficient Network Traffic Classification via Pre-training Unidirectional Mamba
authors: Tongze Wang, Xiaohui Xie, Wenduo Wang, Chuyi Wang, Youjian Zhao, Yong Cui
input_representation: byte-level multimodal flow representation (MFR-style byte matrix), unidirectional state-space model
relevance: NetMamba swaps the transformer for a unidirectional Mamba SSM pre-trained MAE-style on byte-level flow representations, matching accuracy at much lower latency; SSMs lack attention maps entirely, which changes what explanation tooling can use.

title: Synthetic Benchmarks for Scientific Research in Explainable Machine Learning (XAI-Bench)
authors: Yang Liu, Sujay Khandagale et al.
relevance: Synthetic tabular benchmark suite with known ground-truth feature importance for scoring LIME/SHAP-family explainers on faithfulness, monotonicity, ROAR-style and GT metrics; directly reusable for flow-feature data.

title: "Will You Find These Shortcuts?" A Protocol for Evaluating the Faithfulness of Input Salience Methods for Text Classification
authors: Jasmijn Bastings et al.
relevance: Injects known shortcuts into training data so ground-truth important features are known, then checks whether salience methods find them; a shortcut-injection protocol transferable to packet/flow classifiers.

title: Improving IoT Security With Explainable AI: Quantitative Evaluation of Explainability for IoT Botnet Detection
authors: Rajesh Kalakoti, Hayretdin Bahsi, Sven Nomm
relevance: Scores LIME/SHAP explanations of IoT botnet detectors with quantitative faithfulness, monotonicity, complexity and sensitivity metrics on N-BaIoT, MedBIoT and BoT-IoT; SHAP wins — the general metrics ported into network security.

title: DeepMAL - Deep Learning Models for Malware Traffic Detection and Classification
authors: Gonzalo Marin, Pedro Casas, German Capdehourat
input_representation: raw bytestream at packet level and flow level (first bytes, no handcrafted features)
relevance: DeepMAL: LSTM+1D-CNN on raw byte streams at both packet and flow granularity for malware traffic (Stratosphere IPS captures), showing raw-flow input (98.6%) beats raw-packet (77.6%) - a clean case study in how input granularity changes what needs explaining.

title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning for Computer Security Applications
authors: Azqa Nadeem, Daniel Vos, Clinton Cao, Luca Pajola, Simon Dieck, Robert Baumgartner, Sicco Verwer
relevance: Systematizes XAI-for-security by stakeholder and pipeline objective; documents that explanation user studies exist in only 14% of security XAI papers and explicitly calls for interpretability-by-design -- the field-level gap statement this angle answers.

title: NetGPT: Generative Pretrained Transformer for Network Traffic
authors: Xuying Meng, Chungang Lin, Yequan Wang, Yujun Zhang
input_representation: hex-encoded header+payload tokens as unified text; field shuffling and prompts
relevance: NetGPT is the first generative (GPT-style) pretrained traffic model supporting both understanding and generation, encoding raw traffic as hex text with header-field shuffling for task adaptation - the generative branch of traffic foundation models.

title: XG-BoT: An Explainable Deep Graph Neural Network for Botnet Detection and Forensics
authors: W. W. Lo, S. Layeghy, M. Sarhan, M. Portmann
explanation_method: GNNExplainer + saliency maps over a grouped-reversible-residual graph isomorphism network
relevance: The reference point for explaining GNN-based network detectors (graph traffic representations are shared with GNN traffic classification).

title: Deep Learning and Traffic Classification: Lessons learned from a commercial-grade dataset with hundreds of encrypted and zero-day applications
relevance: Commercial-grade study of DL traffic classification that treats zero-day (unknown-app) traffic as a first-class problem and shows DL feature extraction helps identify unknown classes at scale.
authors: Lixuan Yang, Alessandro Finamore, Feng Jun, Dario Rossi

title: A Comparative Study of Faithfulness Metrics for Model Interpretability Methods
authors: Chun Sik Chan, Huanqi Kong et al.
relevance: Directly measures that different faithfulness metrics produce conflicting preferences over interpretation methods and proposes meta-criteria (diagnosticity, time complexity) for choosing among metrics.

title: SoK: Pragmatic Assessment of Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese, Pavel Laskov, Johannes Schneider
relevance: Argues research evaluations are too narrow to estimate the operational value of ML-NIDS (hardware, preprocessing, and deployment factors neglected) and proposes 'pragmatic assessment', validated with practitioner surveys.

title: DI-NIDS: Domain Invariant Network Intrusion Detection System
authors: Siamak Layeghy, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Marius Portmann
relevance: Uses domain-adversarial networks (DANN with gradient reversal) to extract domain-invariant flow features and improve cross-dataset NIDS performance - the main domain-adaptation answer to the generalization gap.

title: Order in the Court: Explainable AI Methods Prone to Disagreement
authors: Michael Neely, Stefan F. Schouten et al.
relevance: Shows rank correlation between attribution methods (LIME, IG, DeepLIFT, Grad-SHAP, attention) is low, so agreement-based evaluation without ground truth is uninformative.

title: Machine Learning (In) Security: A Stream of Problems
authors: Fabricio Ceschin, Marcus Botacin, Albert Bifet, Bernhard Pfahringer, Luiz S. Oliveira, Heitor Murilo Gomes, Andre Gregio
venue: ACM Digital Threats: Research and Practice
relevance: Positions cybersecurity data as inherently drifting/evolving streams with delayed labels and adversarial pressure, and offers a checklist for drift-aware security ML.

title: Errors in the CICIDS2017 Dataset and the Significant Differences in Detection Performances It Makes
authors: Maxime Lanvin, Pierre-Francois Gimenez, Yufei Han, Frederic Majorczyk, Ludovic Me, Eric Totel
relevance: Independently finds further CICIDS2017 errors (mislabeled port-scan and botnet flows, duplicated packets) and quantifies how much detection scores change once labels are fixed - direct evidence that reported NIDS accuracy tracks dataset defects.

title: Machine Learning in Network Intrusion Detection: A Cross-Dataset Generalization Study
authors: Marco Cantone, Claudio Marrocco, Alessandro Bria
relevance: Large controlled study showing ML-NIDS performance collapses when train and test come from different datasets even with harmonized NetFlow features, quantifying the generalization gap the single-dataset literature hides.

title: Fine-grained TLS services classification with reject option
authors: Jan Luxemburk, Tomas Cejka
relevance: Large-scale (141M flows, CESNET-TLS22) fine-grained service classification arguing the reject option is essential for deployment because training sets can never contain all classes of a dynamic Internet.

title: XG-NID: Dual-Modality Network Intrusion Detection using a Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network and Large Language Model
relevance: Heterogeneous flow+packet graph NIDS whose explanations are rendered as human-readable rationales via an LLM layer -- the emerging GNN-plus-LLM answer to explanation delivery in intrusion detection.
authors: Y. Farrukh et al. (per arXiv listing)

title: Towards Better Understanding Attribution Methods
authors: Sukrut Rao, Moritz Bohle et al.
relevance: Proposes DiFull/DiPart controlled settings (provably unused regions) plus aggregate ranking, and shows evaluation outcomes flip with protocol settings, further evidence of protocol sensitivity.

title: A Lightweight, Efficient and Explainable-by-Design Convolutional Neural Network for Internet Traffic Classification (LEXNet)
authors: Kevin Fauvel, Alessandro Finamore, Lixuan Yang, Fuxing Chen, Dario Rossi
relevance: A leading explainable-by-design traffic classifier; represents the kind of XAI-NTC model whose explanations the attacks in this corpus target, and a hub for the broader corpus.

title: The Meta-Evaluation Problem in Explainable AI: Identifying Reliable Estimators with MetaQuantus
authors: Anna Hedstrom, Philine Bommer et al.
relevance: States outright that competing quality estimators for the same property 'frequently present conflicting rankings' and proposes meta-evaluating metrics via resilience to noise and reactivity to adversaries; the framework for justifying metric choices.

title: TrafficLLM: Enhancing Large Language Models for Network Traffic Analysis with Generic Traffic Representation
input_representation: traffic-domain tokenization of raw traffic + natural-language instructions (dual-stage LLM fine-tuning)
relevance: TrafficLLM adapts general LLMs to traffic via traffic-domain tokenization and dual-stage instruction/representation tuning with parameter-efficient adaptation, generalizing across detection and generation tasks - the LLM-adaptation branch of the base-model landscape.

title: netFound: Foundation Model for Network Security (Principled Design for Network Foundation Models)
authors: Satyandra Guthula, Roman Beltiukov, Navya Battula, Wenbo Guo, Arpit Gupta
input_representation: protocol-aware tokenized packet headers + flow metadata (IATs, bytes) with burst-flow hierarchical attention; privacy-by-construction (payload-light)
relevance: netFound pre-trains a hierarchical burst-flow transformer with protocol-aware tokenization on a billion-token telemetry corpus (weights and pipeline released); its 'principled design' axes - tokenization, hierarchy, context embedding - define what a faithful explanation of a traffic FM must respect.

title: AnoShift: A Distribution Shift Benchmark for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
authors: Marius Dragoi, Elena Burceanu, Emanuela Haller, Andrei Manolache, Florin Brad
relevance: Benchmark over 10 years of Kyoto-2006+ NIDS traffic with IID/NEAR/FAR temporal splits, showing consistent performance collapse on FAR years across models from Isolation Forest to masked language models.

title: TrafficGPT: Breaking the Token Barrier for Efficient Long Traffic Analysis and Generation
input_representation: long byte-token sequences (~12k tokens) with linear attention over flows
relevance: TrafficGPT extends generative traffic pre-training to ~12k-token flows via linear attention, jointly serving classification and generation; addresses the token-length ceiling that truncates most byte-input models (a hidden input-representation bias XAI should surface).

title: Bad Design Smells in Benchmark NIDS Datasets
authors: Robert Flood, Gints Engelen, David Aspinall, Lieven Desmet
relevance: Systematizes recurring generation-pipeline defects ('design smells') across benchmark NIDS datasets - trivially predictive single features, tooling artifacts, unrealistic attack mixes - unifying the CICIDS-style error reports into a general critique.

title: Evaluating Feature Attribution Methods in the Image Domain
authors: Arne Gevaert, Axel-Jan Rousseau et al.
relevance: Large-scale study showing attribution metrics measure different underlying concepts and rankings vary across metrics and datasets; recommends reporting metric ensembles, advice that transfers to traffic data.

title: Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers
authors: Giorgio Severi, Jim Meyer, Scott Coull, Alina Oprea
relevance: Turns SHAP explanations into an attack tool: uses feature-attribution to pick clean-label backdoor triggers for EMBER/Drebin/Contagio malware classifiers; canonical 'explanation-guided attack' in security.

title: Revisiting Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
authors: Gal Yona, Daniel Greenfeld
relevance: Critiques the randomization sanity check itself, showing its verdicts can reflect task and architecture artifacts rather than genuine explanation failure, i.e. even the sanity checks are unreliable.

title: F-Fidelity: A Robust Framework for Faithfulness Evaluation of Explainable AI
authors: Xu Zheng, Farhad Shirani et al.
relevance: Identifies OOD corruption and information leakage in fidelity/ROAR-style evaluation and fixes both via explanation-agnostic fine-tuning plus random masking; evaluated on image, time-series and NLP models.

title: Revolutionizing Encrypted Traffic Classification with MH-Net: A Multi-View Heterogeneous Graph Model
authors: Haozhen Zhang et al.
input_representation: multi-view heterogeneous traffic graphs: bits aggregated into traffic units at multiple granularities
relevance: MH-Net (TFE-GNN successors) aggregates different numbers of bits into 'traffic units' forming multi-view heterogeneous graphs trained with contrastive multi-task learning; state of the art of the graph-input family.

title: Logic Traps in Evaluating Attribution Scores
authors: Yiming Ju, Yuanzhe Zhang et al.
relevance: Systematically catalogs logical flaws (hidden assumptions, circularity, OOD effects) in common attribution-evaluation practices and warns that conclusions drawn from them can be spurious.

title: Establishing the Contaminating Effect of Metadata Feature Inclusion in Machine-Learned Network Intrusion Detection Models
authors: Laurens D'hooge, Miel Verkerken, Bruno Volckaert, Tim Wauters, Filip De Turck
relevance: Shows that metadata features (IPs, ports, timestamps) act as label proxies in CIC and other benchmark datasets, inflating scores - a concrete, named instance of classifiers keying on dataset artifacts rather than attack behavior.

title: Evaluating Explainable AI for Deep Learning-Based Network Intrusion Detection System Alert Classification
authors: Rajesh Kalakoti, Risto Vaarandi et al.
relevance: Evaluates multiple XAI methods on NIDS alert-prioritization models with quantitative explanation-quality metrics, extending the faithfulness-measurement program to SOC alert triage.

title: ReCDA: Concept Drift Adaptation with Representation Enhancement for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Shuo Yang, Xinran Zheng, Jinze Li, et al.
relevance: Recent top-venue NIDS drift adaptation via self-supervised representation enhancement and robust fine-tuning under scarce labels.

title: Sanity Simulations for Saliency Methods (SMERF)
authors: Joon Sik Kim, Gregory Plumb et al.
relevance: Synthetic benchmarking framework with fully controlled model reasoning; shows saliency methods fail even simple ground-truth-known detection tasks, calibrating how much to trust them elsewhere.

title: Benchmarking the Benchmark -- Analysis of Synthetic NIDS Datasets
authors: Siamak Layeghy, Marcus Gallagher, Marius Portmann
venue: arXiv preprint / Journal of Information Security and Applications
relevance: Statistically compares benign traffic in synthetic NIDS benchmarks (CIC/UNSW lineage) against two real-world networks and finds significant distributional divergence, undermining the external validity of results trained on synthetic testbeds.

title: Sustaining the High Performance of AI-Based Network Traffic Classification Models
authors: Jielun Zhang, Fuhao Li, Feng Ye
relevance: Addresses keeping AI traffic classifiers performant as the application mix changes (new/unseen apps), i.e. model sustainability under open-world class evolution in ToN-level traffic classification.

title: Lens: A Knowledge-Guided Foundation Model for Network Traffic
authors: Xiaochang Li et al.
input_representation: raw traffic as text: plain-text header fields + encrypted payload bytes, T5 encoder-decoder
relevance: Lens is a T5-based traffic foundation model whose knowledge-guided pretraining mixes plain-text protocol headers with encrypted payload bytes across understanding and generation tasks - representative of the encoder-decoder FM branch.

title: Replication: Contrastive Learning and Data Augmentation in Traffic Classification Using a Flowpic Input Representation
authors: Alessandro Finamore, Chao Wang, Jonatan Krolikowski, Jose M. Navarro, Fuxing Chen, Dario Rossi
relevance: The flagship reproducibility study in deep-learning traffic classification: reproducing an IMC'22 flowpic paper on UCDAVIS19/ISCX-VPN/ISCX-Tor plus three more datasets, it uncovers a data-shift/leakage problem in the original and notes most TC literature ships no code artifacts.

title: Incorporating Attribution Importance for Improving Faithfulness Metrics
authors: Zhixue Zhao et al.
relevance: Replaces hard top-k erasure with soft, importance-weighted perturbation (soft comprehensiveness/sufficiency), fixing the arbitrary-threshold weakness of ERASER-style metrics.

title: Evaluating Feature Relevance XAI in Network Intrusion Detection
authors: (Tritscher group, LSX-UniWue — see Springer page)
relevance: Directly evaluates SHAP-style feature-relevance explanations of network intrusion detectors quantitatively; one of the few papers doing rigorous XAI evaluation specifically on NIDS traffic data.

title: A Causal Lens for Evaluating Faithfulness Metrics
authors: Kerem Zaman, Shashank Srivastava et al.
relevance: Meta-evaluates faithfulness metrics with model-editing-based ground truth (Causal Diagnosticity); finds most metrics perform near chance at diagnosing which of two explanations is faithful.

title: A Fresh Look at Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
authors: Anna Hedstrom, Leander Weber et al.
relevance: Responds to documented methodological concerns about the Model Parameter Randomisation Test with Smooth-MPRT and Efficient-MPRT variants; part of the metric-repair literature.

title: Normalized AOPC: Fixing Misleading Faithfulness Metrics for Feature Attribution Explainability
authors: Joakim Edin, Andreas Geert Motzfeldt et al.
relevance: Proves AOPC scores are model-dependent so cross-model faithfulness comparisons are invalid, and proposes normalized AOPC; important when comparing explanations across different traffic-classifier architectures.

title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time (Extended Version)
authors: Zeliang Kan, Shae McFadden, Daniel Arp, Feargus Pendlebury, Roberto Jordaney, Johannes Kinder, Fabio Pierazzi, Lorenzo Cavallaro
relevance: Updated TESSERACT with the AUT robustness metric and constraints for fair experiment design, extending the temporal/spatial-bias argument beyond Android malware.

title: A Feasible and Explainable Network Traffic Classifier Utilizing DistilBERT
relevance: Distilled traffic BERT with an explicit XAI pass that maps learned feature importance back onto packet-structure positions ('analyzed the relationships between the features by associating them with the packet structure') -- one of the few transformer-for-traffic papers with a dedicated explanation analysis.

title: The Attention-Based Autoencoder for Network Traffic Classification with Interpretable Feature Representation (AMAE)
relevance: Builds attention into an autoencoder expressly so the attention over global spatial structure yields interpretable feature representations of traffic classes -- attention-as-explanation by construction, again without faithfulness testing.

title: The Solvability of Interpretability Evaluation Metrics
authors: Yilun Zhou, Julie Shah
relevance: Shows comprehensiveness/sufficiency are 'solvable': beam search can construct explanations that maximize the metric while ignoring the model's reasoning, so metric-topping methods may just be gaming the metric.

title: The Disagreement Problem in Faithfulness Metrics
authors: Brian Barr, Noah Fatsi et al.
relevance: Shows on tabular data that faithfulness metrics themselves disagree about which explanation method is best; exactly the requested evidence that the measuring sticks are mutually inconsistent.

title: Hybrid attention-enhanced explainable model for encrypted traffic detection and classification
relevance: Recent journal paper coupling hybrid attention modules with an explainability component for encrypted traffic detection -- representative of the 2025 wave that treats attention outputs as the explanation artifact.

title: MIETT: Multi-Instance Encrypted Traffic Transformer for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Xu-Yang Chen et al.
input_representation: flow as bag of packets; hex byte tokens with two-level (token-level + packet-level) attention
relevance: MIETT treats a flow as a multi-instance bag of packets with dual-level attention and packet-order/contrastive pre-training tasks, capturing both token and packet relationships - the two-level attention structure is exactly what attention-based explanations need to respect.

title: MM4flow: A Pre-trained Multi-modal Model for Versatile Network Traffic Analysis
input_representation: multi-modal: byte content + flow-level modalities pre-trained jointly
relevance: MM4flow (CCS'25) is a pre-trained multi-modal traffic model unifying content and flow modalities for versatile downstream analysis - the newest top-venue entry in the traffic foundation-model line.

title: Multi-Task Scenario Encrypted Traffic Classification and Parameter Analysis (PETReLM)
relevance: LoRA fine-tuning of a BERT traffic model with a transformer-internals analysis: SVD of query-projection matrices across layers shows lower layers filter task-relevant representations while higher layers process abstract features -- weight-level (not attention-level) interpretability of a traffic transformer; future work names 'deeper interpretability'.

title: On the Coherency of Quantitative Evaluation of Visual Explanations
authors: Benjamin Vandersmissen, Jose Oramas
relevance: Empirically finds different evaluation methods grade the same explanations inconsistently and that properties like sparsity confound scores; more direct evidence of inter-metric incoherence.

title: The Blame Problem in Evaluating Local Explanations, and How to Tackle It
authors: Amir Hossein Akhavan Rahnama
relevance: Argues the bar for new explainers is low because evaluation measures are weak, and that most metrics cannot separate explanation error from model/data artifacts (the 'blame problem').

title: TE-G-SAGE: Explainable Edge-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Network Intrusion Detection
relevance: Edge-aware GNN NIDS designed for interpretability, motivated by the observation that graph models 'are frequently difficult to interpret, in contrast to many classical approaches' -- provides edge-level explanations on NetFlow benchmark graphs.

title: X-CBA: Explainability Aided CatBoosted Anomal-E for Intrusion Detection System
relevance: Couples the self-supervised Anomal-E GNN pipeline with explainability (PFI/SHAP-style local-global analysis) for edge-embedding-based NIDS -- explicit attempt to make GNN NIDS decisions analyst-legible.
authors: K. Neshenko et al. (per arXiv listing)

title: Discovering Non-Metadata Contaminant Features in Intrusion Detection Datasets
authors: Laurens D'hooge, Miel Verkerken, Tim Wauters, Bruno Volckaert, Filip De Turck
relevance: Follow-up showing contamination is not limited to obvious metadata: derived flow features (e.g., TTL-related and size statistics) also leak labels in benchmark IDS datasets, so simple feature-dropping does not fix shortcut learning.

title: Demystifying Network Foundation Models
relevance: First systematic interpretability audit of traffic foundation models (cites both ET-BERT and YaTC): probes hidden representations via embedding geometry, alignment with domain-expert features, and causal protocol perturbations, finding 'significant anisotropy, inconsistent feature sensitivity patterns, an inability to separate the high-level context, [and] payload dependency' across all four NFMs tested.

title: Evaluating Explainability of Graph Neural Networks for Network Intrusion Detection with Structural Attacks
authors: Dimitri Galli, Andrea Venturi, Isabella Marasco, Mirco Marchetti
relevance: Rare head-to-head evaluation of five XAI techniques on GNN-based NIDS without ground-truth explanations, using explanation-guided structural attacks as the yardstick; finds Integrated Gradients most accurate -- and shows accurate explanations double as attacker reconnaissance.
_key: t:evaluating explainability of graph neural networks for network intrusion detection with structural attacks

title: Explainable But Vulnerable: Adversarial Attacks on XAI Explanation in Cybersecurity Applications
authors: Maraz Mia, et al.
venue: IEEE TPS-ISA (Trust, Privacy and Security in Intelligent Systems and Applications)
relevance: Systematically studies fairwashing, manipulation, and backdoor attacks on SHAP, LIME and Integrated Gradients specifically in cybersecurity classifiers.

title: Evaluation of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in IoT Intrusion Detection Systems Under DeepFool Adversarial Conditions
authors: Munilla et al.
relevance: Benchmarks SHAP and LIME robustness for IoT IDS under DeepFool attacks, quantifying trade-offs in feature alignment and explanation stability.

title: Cross-Domain Generalization Failure in Lightweight Intrusion Detection Models for IIoT Networks
relevance: Documents cross-domain generalization failure specifically for lightweight IIoT IDS models, extending the XeNIDS/Layeghy finding to the resource-constrained regime.
authors: MD Azizul Hakim, Md Shihab Uddin, Talha Ibne Anis

title: One task to rule them all: A closer look at traffic classification generalizability
authors: Elham Akbari, Zihao Zhou, Mohammad A. Salahuddin, Noura Limam, Raouf Boutaba, et al.
input_representation: cross-task/cross-dataset evaluation of standard input representations
relevance: Empirically tests whether traffic classifiers generalize across tasks and datasets (largely: they do not), quantifying the external-validity gap that shortcut-hunting explanations try to localize.

title: Investigating the Impact of Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Model Explanation in IoT-based DDoS Detection Systems
authors: Mahmood et al.
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science & Technology (IJIST)
relevance: Measures how adversarial evasion perturbations degrade the consistency/stability of SHAP-LIME explanations in IoT DDoS detectors -- attack-on-explanation in the traffic domain.

title: Are Explanations Robust to Federated Poisoning? An Empirical Study in Cyber Threat Detection
authors: Bakhtiari et al.
venue: SECRYPT (Int. Conf. on Security and Cryptography)
relevance: Studies how federated poisoning attacks degrade the reliability of Integrated Gradients, SHAP and LIME across cyber-threat detection models.

title: PLAA: Packet-level Adversarial Attacks in Network Traffic Detection
authors: You et al.
relevance: Constructs packet-level adversarial traffic that preserves validity and semantic integrity, reporting ~92.8% average evasion across datasets -- a realistic problem-space traffic attack.

title: Controllability-Aware Adversarial Examples Against LLM-Based Network Traffic Classifiers
authors: Li et al.
relevance: Black-box transfer attack that partitions flow features by attacker controllability to evade emerging LLM-based traffic classifiers; shows LLM classifiers carry substantial transfer vulnerability.

title: Neurosymbolic Learning for Advanced Persistent Threat Detection (BERT + Logic Tensor Networks)
relevance: Unifies BERT with Logic Tensor Networks for explainable APT detection in class-imbalanced IoT networks -- differentiable first-order logic constraints as the interpretability mechanism.

title: Explaining Intrusion Alert Decisions of Deep Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems for Security Analysts (EXP-SEC)
authors: Ayush Kumar, Vrizlynn L.L. Thing
relevance: Feature-GROUP attributions multi-stage-mapped into domain-level, SOC-analyst-friendly explanations; argues analysts need interdependency-aware, semantic explanations rather than isolated per-feature attribution -- the bridge from attribution toward concept-level explanation for NIDS.

title: Human-Centered Explainability in AI-Enhanced UI Security Interfaces
authors: Mona Rajhans
relevance: Mixed-methods user study comparing explanation styles (including counterfactuals) in cybersecurity dashboards on trust and decision accuracy -- rare human-subjects evidence about which explanation FORM security users actually benefit from.

title: ShortcutCatcher: Making Traffic Classification Reliable
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Networking
relevance: Uses explainable-AI attribution to automatically detect and mitigate shortcut learning in traffic classifiers by contrasting model behavior across a training and a differently-collected verification dataset -- XAI as a debugging instrument for exactly the models in this corpus.

title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification (BiasSeeker)
relevance: Semi-automated, model-agnostic shortcut/bias discovery for encrypted-traffic classifiers; motivated by the observation that 'existing solutions heavily rely on model-specific interpretation techniques, which lack adaptability and generality across different model architectures'.
authors: Chuyi Wang et al.

title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Honglei Jin et al.
relevance: Concept-bottleneck alternative to post-hoc explanation for traffic (cites ET-BERT and YaTC as opaque baselines): organizes flow statistics, packet sequences and byte representations into an explicit concept space because existing fusions yield 'opaque latent features, making it unclear which type of evidence actually drives the prediction'.

title: Online Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems with Explainable Concept Drift Detection and Adaptation Phases
authors: Drago et al.
relevance: Directly on the angle: an online IDS framework whose concept-drift detection and adaptation phases are made explainable, from the group behind several drift-aware IDS systems (HOIDS).
_key: t:online framework for intrusion detection systems with explainable concept drift detection and adaptation phases

title: Beyond Detection Accuracy: Measuring Explanation Cost, Stability, and Utility for Resource-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection
authors: Abdurrahman Tolay
relevance: Measures local explanation STABILITY (TreeSHAP) alongside cost and utility for LR/DT/RF/XGBoost IDS on a leakage-safe CICIoT2023 split; finds RF most explanation-stable while XGBoost shows top-feature turnover and attribution-magnitude drift.

title: Can SHAP-Based Explanations Differentiate Between Concept Drift and Scale Drift in Computer Networks Data?
relevance: Asks the angle's question head-on: under pure scale drift classifier performance degrades while TreeSHAP attribution distributions remain stable, so monitoring SHAP distributions can distinguish drift types in network data.

title: SymbXRL: Symbolic Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Networks
authors: Abhishek Duttagupta, Claudio Fiandrino, et al.
relevance: Synthesizes human-interpretable symbolic explanations (symbols + logical rules) for DRL agents managing 6G resource allocation, and uses them for intent-based programmatic action steering that improves cumulative reward by ~12% over pure DRL.

title: LEAD-Drift: Real-time and Explainable Intent Drift Detection by Learning a Data-Driven Risk Score
authors: Md. Kamrul Hossain, et al.
relevance: Neural risk score for intent drift in Intent-Based Networking with SHAP-based per-alert explanations that identify root-cause KPIs, achieving 7.3-minute average lead time and 80.2% alert-noise reduction - joins explainability with operational root-cause analysis.

title: TunnelEye: An Explainable Framework for Real-Time Detection of Malicious DoH Traffic in High-Speed Backbone Networks
authors: Jiajia Du, et al.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
relevance: Argues existing DoH detectors' generic bidirectional statistics 'lack interpretability, are costly to compute, and may become unavailable or unstable' under backbone sampling; proposes protocol-level behavioral features stable across directions plus a DoH-Sketch data structure for real-time explainable detection.

title: Stabilising Explainability Fragility in Cybersecurity AI: The Impact and Mitigation of Multicollinearity in Public Benchmark Datasets
authors: (authors per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Analysis of SHAP/LIME instability under multicollinearity across linear, tree, kernel and neural models
relevance: Shows correlated flow features make attributions non-identifiable - a fundamental validity threat for every SHAP-on-flow-features paper, traffic classification included.

title: Revealing the Vulnerabilities of Learning-based Network Intrusion Detectors through XAI-guided Adversarial Attack
authors: Li et al.
relevance: Bullseye: uses SHAP and LIME to guide efficient adversarial traffic generation against learning-based NIDS, directly linking explanation attribution to evasion of traffic classifiers.

title: FATFI: A Framework to Generate Adversarial Traffic with Feature Interpretability
authors: (Springer chapter)
relevance: Bullseye: multi-level (global+local) explanation methods score feature importance to choose optimal perturbation strategies for generating adversarial network traffic.

title: Explainable AI-Based Intrusion Detection Systems for Industry 5.0 and Adversarial XAI: A Systematic Review
authors: (MDPI Information systematic review)
relevance: Systematic review at the exact intersection: XAI-based IDS plus 'adversarial XAI', surveying how explanations for traffic/security classifiers are attacked and defended.

title: CANDICE: An explainable and intelligent framework for network intrusion detection
authors: Shuhua Li, Ruiying Du, Jing Chen, Kun He, Cong Wu, Yebo Feng
relevance: Generates counterfactual explanations for NIDS decisions by disentangling traffic representations and optimizing a multi-objective loss under security-specific constraints, then compiles them into per-attack intrusion profiles; reports superior fidelity/sparsity/stability at >96.1% detection accuracy.
_key: t:candice an explainable and intelligent framework for network intrusion detection

title: Tabular Diffusion based Actionable Counterfactual Explanations for Network Intrusion Detection (journal: Novel Actionable Counterfactual Explanations for Intrusion Detection Using Diffusion Models)
authors: Vinura Galwaduge, Jagath Samarabandu
venue: arXiv / Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy 5(3):68
relevance: Diffusion-based generator of minimal, diverse, ACTIONABLE counterfactuals for NIDS, claiming the first comparative benchmark of counterfactual algorithms (DiCE-style baselines) on three modern intrusion datasets, and converting counterfactuals into global filtering rules.

title: ProvX: Generating Counterfactual-Driven Attack Explanations for Provenance-Based Detection
authors: Weiheng Wu, Wei Qiao, Teng Li, Yebo Feng, Zhuo Ma, Jianfeng Ma, Yang Liu
relevance: Counterfactual (minimal graph perturbation) explanations for GNN-based provenance intrusion detection, reporting average explanation necessity of 51.59% -- counterfactual reasoning transplanted to security detection graphs.

title: eX-NIDS: A Framework for Explainable Network Intrusion Detection Leveraging Large Language Models
authors: Paul R. B. Houssel, Siamak Layeghy, Priyanka Singh, Marius Portmann
relevance: LLM (Llama 3 / GPT-4) natural-language explanations of NetFlow alerts, with a Prompt Augmenter injecting CTI and context that improves explanation correctness/consistency >20% over naive prompting -- defines an evaluation method for NL explanations of NIDS.

title: Neurosymbolic AI for network intrusion detection systems: A survey
authors: Alice Bizzarri, Brian Jalaian, et al.
venue: Journal of Information Security and Applications, vol. 94
relevance: Survey categorizing neurosymbolic NIDS approaches into logic-based and graph-based representations -- the map of the NeSy-for-NIDS sub-literature and its claimed interpretability benefits.
_key: t:neurosymbolic ai for network intrusion detection systems a survey

title: Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence for Robust Network Intrusion Detection: From Scratch to Transfer Learning
authors: Tran et al. (with Brian Jalaian group)
relevance: Concrete neurosymbolic NIDS combining neural learning with symbolic reasoning for robustness and transfer across network environments -- an actual system (not survey) in the NeSy-NIDS thread.

title: Designing a neuro-symbolic dual-model architecture for explainable and resilient intrusion detection in IoT networks
authors: (Scientific Reports 2025; see article page)
relevance: Dual-model neuro-symbolic IDS (e.g., RF/SNN plus symbolic reasoning) for IoT networks producing interpretable, actionable alerts -- shows symbolic layers being used as the explanation carrier in deployed-style IDS.

title: Building Transparency in Deep Learning-Powered Network Traffic Classification: A Traffic-Explainer Framework
relevance: Model-agnostic input-perturbation explainer (mutual-information-maximizing masks over sequential traffic inputs) for DL traffic models -- explicitly built because operators distrust opaque models; sidesteps attention rather than validating it.
authors: Riya Ponraj, Ram Durairajan et al.

title: Drift-Based Dataset Stability Benchmark
authors: Dominik Soukup, Richard Plny, Daniel Vasata, Tomas Cejka
relevance: Proposes a dataset-stability benchmark combining concept-drift detection with ML feature weights, demonstrated on CESNET-TLS-Year22, to predict when deployed traffic classifiers will degrade.

title: LAMDA: A Longitudinal Android Malware Benchmark for Concept Drift Analysis
relevance: 12-year, 1M+ sample drift benchmark that explicitly quantifies EXPLANATION DRIFT via Jaccard and Kendall distances over SHAP attributions - showing the features a detector relies on shift over time even when accuracy holds.

title: TrafficFormer: An Efficient Pre-trained Model for Traffic Data
authors: Guangmeng Zhou et al.
input_representation: raw-byte field tokens; fine-grained multi-classification pretext + random-initialization field augmentation
relevance: TrafficFormer (S&P'25) strengthens ET-BERT-style pre-training with a fine-grained flow-similarity pretext task and field-randomizing augmentation to 'focus on key information' - the current top venue-validated pre-trained ETC model and a prime explanation target.
_key: t:trafficformer an efficient pre trained model for traffic data

title: The Sweet Danger of Sugar: Debunking Representation Learning for Encrypted Traffic Classification (Pcap-Encoder)
authors: Yuqi Zhao et al.
input_representation: critique of raw-byte inputs; proposes Pcap-Encoder, an LM that extracts features from protocol headers only
relevance: Debunks byte-level representation-learning ETC: shows benchmark artifacts (header leftovers) rather than payload semantics drive reported accuracy, and that a header-focused LM (Pcap-Encoder) suffices - the strongest published statement of the shortcut-learning problem XAI-for-traffic must detect.

title: On the Effect of Ruleset Tuning and Data Imbalance on Explainable Network Security Alert Classifications: a Case-Study on DeepCASE
authors: Koen T. W. Teuwen, Sam Baggen, Emmanuele Zambon, Luca Allodi
relevance: Shows SOC label imbalance and detection-rule tuning materially change both performance AND the correctness of the explanations DeepCASE-style systems give analysts -- explanation quality is an operational variable, not a fixed property.

title: Feature Attribution in 5G Intrusion Detection: A Statistical vs. Logic-Based Comparison
authors: Federica Uccello, Simin Nadjm-Tehrani
relevance: Head-to-head SHAP vs. logic-based VoTE-XAI attribution for 5G intrusion detection including explanation-generation speed for real-time security monitoring; finds logic-based attributions sparser, more stable, and faster.

title: XAInomaly: Explainable and interpretable Deep Contractive Autoencoder for O-RAN traffic anomaly detection
authors: Osman Tugay Basaran, Falko Dressler
relevance: Semi-supervised deep contractive autoencoder for O-RAN traffic anomaly detection paired with fastSHAP-C, a resource-aware SHAP variant designed for real-time explanation inside near-RT RIC constraints - representative of the 'lightweight XAI for 6G' thread.

title: BEAR: BGP Event Analysis and Reporting
authors: Hanqing Li, et al.
relevance: LLM-based multi-step reasoning that turns tabular BGP telemetry into explanatory natural-language reports for anomalies such as route leaks and hijacks - the emerging 'LLM as explainer' pattern for network operations, including a synthetic data generation framework.

title: Integrating Explainable AI for Effective Malware Detection in Encrypted Network Traffic
authors: Sileshi Nibret Zeleke, et al.
relevance: Ensemble (XGBoost, 99.32% acc.) over multi-view features of encrypted malicious traffic (custom 1,127-connection dataset spanning 54 malware families, benchmarked on CTU-13) with SHAP identifying max packet size, mean inter-arrival time and TLS version as decisive features.

title: From Flows to Functions: Macroscopic Behavioral Fingerprinting of IoT Devices via Network Services
authors: Shayan Azizi, et al.
relevance: Explicitly positions service-level IoT device identification as 'macroscopic, lightweight, and explainable' versus packet-level deep learning, validated on 13 consumer IoT device types over 10M IPFIX flow records spanning 1.5 years - interpretable-by-design device fingerprinting.

title: ClearNET: Enhancing Transparency in Opaque Network Models Using Explainable AI (XAI) for Efficient Traffic Engineering
authors: Cristian Zilli, et al.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
relevance: Applies XAI to data-driven traffic engineering and telemetry, examining intrinsic model behavior to cut the volume of telemetry data needed for learning; authors note XAI use 'in computer network management remains largely unexplored'.

title: Interpretable Anomaly Detection in Encrypted Traffic Using SHAP with Machine Learning Models
authors: (authors per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: SHAP over multiple ML classifiers
relevance: Direct bridge paper: SHAP-based interpretation on encrypted traffic features, i.e., the exact feature space of encrypted traffic classification.

title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
authors: Maximilian Noppel, Christian Wressnegger
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)
relevance: Systematization-of-knowledge that organizes threat models and attacks against explanations in security settings; a taxonomy hub for this angle and a source of open-problem statements.
_key: t:sok explainable machine learning in adversarial environments

title: Adversarial attacks and defenses in explainable artificial intelligence: A survey
authors: Hubert Baniecki, Przemyslaw Biecek
relevance: The field-defining survey of adversarial XAI, with unified notation/taxonomy over attacks on explanations and defenses; the best single map for citation expansion on this angle.

title: Explainability Guided Adversarial Evasion Attacks on Malware Detectors
authors: Kshitiz Aryal, Maanak Gupta, Mahmoud Abdelsalam, et al.
relevance: Uses SHAP to locate decision-critical regions of PE malware and injects perturbations there, showing explanation-guided perturbation is far more efficient than random placement for evasion.

title: Problem space structural adversarial attacks for Network Intrusion Detection Systems based on Graph Neural Networks
authors: Andrea Venturi, et al.
relevance: Formalizes problem-space constraints for GNN-based NIDS; finds GNNs resist feature-based attacks but remain vulnerable to structure-based (graph-topology) perturbations.

title: Rules Refine the Riddle: Global Explanation for Deep Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Security Applications (GEAD)
authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Ruitao Feng, Minghui Jin, Wenqi Chen, Kai Wang, Su Wang, Jiahai Yang, Xingang Shi, Xia Yin, et al.
relevance: Global rule extraction from DL anomaly detectors via root regression tree generation plus low-confidence region identification/augmentation -- the CCS follow-up to DeepAID moving from local reference-based to global rule-based explanation.

title: Dissect Black Box: Interpreting for Rule-Based Explanations in Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
authors: Yu Zhang, Ruoyu Li, Nengwu Wu, Qing Li, Xinhan Lin, Yang Hu, Tao Li, Yong Jiang
relevance: Follow-on rule-based explanation of unsupervised anomaly detectors using a Segmentation Clustering Decision Tree plus Gaussian Boundary Delineation, decomposing normal-traffic distributions into rules.
_key: t:dissect black box interpreting for rule based explanations in unsupervised anomaly detection

title: Genos: General In-Network Unsupervised Intrusion Detection by Rule Extraction
authors: Ruoyu Li, Qing Li, Yu Zhang, Dan Zhao, Xi Xiao, Yong Jiang
relevance: Pushes rule extraction from unsupervised NIDS models all the way into the data plane: extracted rules run at 100 Gbps on programmable switches, showing surrogate rules are not just explanations but deployable artifacts.

title: Eclectic Rule Extraction for Explainability of Deep Neural Network based Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Jesse Ables, Nathaniel Childers, William Anderson, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi, Ioana Banicescu, Maria Seale
relevance: Combines pedagogical and decompositional rule extraction on DNN IDS models, reaching 99.9% fidelity rulesets on UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS-2017 -- a concrete X-IDS instantiation of rule extraction on standard NIDS datasets.

title: Validating network attack concepts: A TCAV-driven approach
authors: R. R. Rejimol Robinson, Rendhir R. Prasad, Ciza Thomas, N. Balakrishnan
venue: Journal of Computer Virology and Hacking Techniques 20:841-855
relevance: The ONLY located application of TCAV concept-based explanation to network attacks: defines attack concepts and measures concept sensitivity on KDD Cup 1999 -- proving feasibility but on a 25-year-old dataset, leaving modern traffic untouched.
_key: t:validating network attack concepts a tcav driven approach

title: A Critical Assessment of Interpretable and Explainable Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
authors: Omer Subasi, Johnathan Cree, Joseph Manzano, Elena Peterson
relevance: Empirically shows feature-based explanations for IDS are inconsistent across methods (introducing 'cross explanations'), blames complex opaque models plus correlated/imbalanced data, and recommends inherently interpretable models -- direct ammunition for beyond-attribution approaches.

title: CESNET-TLS-Year22: A year-spanning TLS network traffic dataset from backbone lines
authors: Karel Hynek, Jan Luxemburk, Jaroslav Pesek, Tomas Cejka, Pavel Siska
relevance: Year-long backbone TLS dataset (180 services, 100Gbps lines) built explicitly to evaluate classifier robustness against temporal drift in production networks - the main public drift benchmark for traffic classification.

title: Combating Concept Drift with Explanatory Detection and Adaptation for Android Malware Classification (DREAM)
relevance: Successor to CADE: embeds explanatory drift detection inside a contrastive autoencoder with expert knowledge, achieving equal accuracy with 76.6% fewer newly labeled samples - explanation used as the drift-handling mechanism itself.

title: Addressing Concept Drift in IoT Anomaly Detection: Drift Detection, Interpretation, and Adaptation (CDDIA)
relevance: Unified framework that detects drift in IoT streams, INTERPRETS drift points, and adapts the model, aimed at cutting the false positives that unexplained normality changes cause.
_key: t:addressing concept drift in iot anomaly detection drift detection interpretation and adaptation cddia

title: AIChronoLens: Advancing Explainability for Time Series AI Forecasting in Mobile Networks
authors: Claudio Fiandrino, Eloy Perez Gomez, Pablo Fernandez Perez, Hossein Mohammadalizadeh, Marco Fiore, Joerg Widmer
relevance: Ties legacy XAI relevance scores to temporal properties (maxima/minima) of the input so explanations of LSTM/transformer traffic-load forecasters for 5G base stations become meaningful; explanation-guided retraining improves prediction error by 32% (39% with meta-learning) on real operator traces.
_key: t:aichronolens advancing explainability for time series ai forecasting in mobile networks

title: SliceOps: Explainable MLOps for Streamlined Automation-Native 6G Networks
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, Sarang Kahvazadeh, et al.
relevance: Embeds an XAI-augmented MLOps loop ('SliceOps') as a standalone slice in 6G architecture, using explanation-guided reinforcement learning for radio resource allocation across slices - joins the XAI and MLOps lifecycles for slicing automation.

title: Toward Explainable Reasoning in 6G: A Proof of Concept Study on Radio Resource Allocation (TANGO)
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, et al.
venue: arXiv (IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society version)
relevance: Couples graph reinforcement learning with a Bayesian-GNN explainer and symbolic reasoning that translates edge/node importance and uncertainty into logical reward terms for gNodeB resource allocation, reporting 96.39% accuracy and 1.22x gains over baselines.

title: Examining the Rat in the Tunnel: Interpretable Multi-Label Classification of Tor-based Malware
authors: Ishan Karunanayake, et al.
relevance: Message-passing neural network classifies Tor-based malware traffic (micro-avg precision/recall >90%) and applies XAI to interpret which traffic patterns distinguish malware classes, plus an adversarial-robustness evaluation - malware-over-anonymity-network detection with explanations.

title: E-XAI: Evaluating Black-Box Explainable AI Frameworks for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: O. Arreche, T. R. Guntur, J. W. Roberts, M. Abdallah
explanation_method: End-to-end evaluation of SHAP and LIME (global + local) across several black-box models with six metrics (descriptive accuracy, sparsity, efficiency, stability, robustness, completeness)
relevance: The most complete quantitative benchmark of SHAP vs LIME for NIDS; its metric suite is directly reusable for traffic-classification explainers.
_key: t:e xai evaluating black box explainable ai frameworks for network intrusion detection

title: Disguising Attacks with Explanation-Aware Backdoors
authors: Maximilian Noppel, Lukas Peter, Christian Wressnegger
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P)
relevance: Backdoors that not only flip predictions but also produce an attacker-chosen, benign-looking explanation, defeating explanation-based inspection/audit defenses.
_key: t:disguising attacks with explanation aware backdoors

title: Evasion Adversarial Attacks Remain Impractical Against ML-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems, Especially Dynamic Ones
authors: Mohamed elShehaby, Ashraf Matrawy
relevance: Threat-models practicality of evasion against ML-NIDS and shows continuous retraining (dynamic learning) sharply cuts attack effectiveness -- a strong research-vs-practice-gap statement.

title: Interpreting Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Security via Rule Extraction
authors: Ruoyu Li, Qing Li, Yu Zhang, Dan Zhao, Yong Jiang, Yong Yang
relevance: Global rule extraction for black-box unsupervised anomaly detection via an Interior Clustering Tree and Compositional Boundary Exploration -- distills network anomaly detectors into human-readable axis-aligned rules.
_key: t:interpreting unsupervised anomaly detection in security via rule extraction

title: Explaining Tree Model Decisions in Natural Language for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Noah Ziems, Gang Liu, John Flanagan, Meng Jiang
relevance: Uses LLMs to turn decision-tree NIDS decision paths into natural-language explanations, evaluated with quiz-based human understanding tests -- a natural-language explanation form layered on interpretable tree models for NIDS.

title: Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection
authors: Yizheng Chen, Zhoujie Ding, David Wagner
relevance: Hierarchical contrastive learning plus uncertainty-based active learning to keep a detector alive over seven years of drift, cutting false negatives from 14% to 9% versus best prior continual-learning baselines.

title: Are Existing Out-Of-Distribution Techniques Suitable for Network Intrusion Detection?
authors: Andrea Corsini, Shanchieh Jay Yang
relevance: Tests six OOD detectors from vision/other domains on unknown attacks in NIDS and finds new attacks are not guaranteed to appear OOD, questioning direct transfer of OOD tooling to traffic.

title: Deep learning for encrypted traffic classification in the face of data drift: An empirical study
authors: Navid Malekghaini, Elham Akbari, Mohammad A. Salahuddin, Noura Limam, Raouf Boutaba, Bertrand Mathieu, Stephanie Moteau, Stephane Tuffin
