relevance: Tracks two SOTA deep ETC models across ISP datasets collected two years apart: accuracy decays in production, retraining only partially recovers it, and traffic-shape features prove more drift-resilient than TLS-header features.
_key: t:deep learning for encrypted traffic classification in the face of data drift an empirical study

title: Rosetta: Enabling Robust TLS Encrypted Traffic Classification in Diverse Network Environments with TCP-Aware Traffic Augmentation
authors: Renjie Xie, Jiahao Cao, Enhuan Dong, Mingwei Xu, Kun Sun, Qi Li, Licheng Shen, Menghao Zhang
input_representation: packet-length sequences of TLS flows, made invariant via TCP-aware augmentation + self-supervised features
relevance: Rosetta shows existing DL classifiers 'all have significant performance degradation in real diverse network environments' because TCP mechanics reshape packet-length sequences, and fixes it with TCP-aware augmentation; key evidence that learned features are fragile artifacts - central to XAI motivation.
_key: t:rosetta enabling robust tls encrypted traffic classification in diverse network environments with tcp aware traffic augmentation

title: MTC: A Multi-Task Model for Encrypted Network Traffic Classification Based on Transformer and 1D-CNN
authors: Kunda Wang, Jia Gao, Xiaoqin Lei
input_representation: raw session bytes fed in parallel to Transformer (long-range) and 1D-CNN (local) branches
relevance: MTC fuses parallel Transformer and 1D-CNN branches over raw bytes for joint app identification and traffic characterization on ISCX VPN-nonVPN (F1 ~98%); a representative hybrid-architecture explained in multi-task XAI settings.
_key: t:mtc a multi task model for encrypted network traffic classification based on transformer and 1d cnn

title: SoK: Pragmatic Assessment of Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese, Pavel Laskov, Johannes Schneider
relevance: Defines 'pragmatic assessment' of ML-NIDS (hundreds of configs, four hardware platforms, runtime/cost reporting) and validates the notion with a user study of security practitioners -- the practitioner-skepticism framing this whole sub-literature answers.

title: EXPLORA: AI/ML EXPLainability for the Open RAN
authors: Claudio Fiandrino, Leonardo Bonati, Salvatore D'Oro, Michele Polese, Tommaso Melodia, Joerg Widmer
relevance: Explains DRL agents controlling the Open RAN via attributed action-graphs, deployed on an O-RAN-compliant testbed (Colosseum) and designed for real-time operation inside RAN control loops -- concrete evidence on explanation latency budgets in production-like networks.

title: TRUST XAI: Model-Agnostic Explanations for AI With a Case Study on IIoT Security
authors: Maede Zolanvari, Zebo Yang, Khaled Khan, Raj Jain, Nader Meskin
relevance: Statistical model-agnostic explainer (factor analysis + mutual information + Gaussian likelihoods) benchmarked on IIoT/network security data; explicitly positions itself as superior to LIME in performance AND speed, targeting online explanation of new samples.

title: Spotting Deep Neural Network Vulnerabilities in Mobile Traffic Forecasting with an Explainable AI Lens (DeExp)
authors: Serly Moghadas Gholian, Claudio Fiandrino, Alan Collet, Giulia Attanasio, Marco Fiore, Joerg Widmer
relevance: Uses Grad-CAM and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation to find which base stations a mobile-traffic-forecasting DNN depends on, showing prediction error grows >400% under moderate adversarial traffic injection - XAI as a vulnerability-audit tool for operational forecasting models.

title: Explanation-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning for Trustworthy 6G RAN Slicing
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, Hatim Chergui, Luis Alonso, Christos Verikoukis
relevance: Uses explanations inside the DRL training loop (explanation-guided reward) for multi-agent inter-slice resource allocation so SLA-meeting slicing decisions stay transparent, directly addressing the opaqueness objection to DRL slice controllers.

title: RADAR: A TTP-based Extensible, Explainable, and Effective System for Network Traffic Analysis and Malware Detection
authors: Yashovardhan Sharma, Simon Birnbach, Ivan Martinovic
relevance: Grounds malware detection from traffic in MITRE ATT&CK TTPs so every alert is explainable in analyst vocabulary rather than opaque model scores - explainability-by-domain-semantics for malware traffic analysis.

title: Investigating the practicality of adversarial evasion attacks on network intrusion detection
authors: Mohamed Amine Merzouk, Frederic Cuppens, Nora Boulahia-Cuppens, Reda Yaich
relevance: Argues classic adversarial-example algorithms produce unrealizable traffic (boolean/discrete features, out-of-range values), a key statement of the feature-space vs problem-space gap for NIDS.

title: XG-BoT: An Explainable Deep Graph Neural Network for Botnet Detection and Forensics
authors: Wai Weng Lo et al.
relevance: Applies GNNExplainer plus saliency maps to a grouped-reversible GNN botnet detector to highlight suspicious flows/nodes for forensics -- the archetype of GNNExplainer-borrowed-into-network-security.

title: On Generalisability of Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann
relevance: Evaluates seven supervised/unsupervised models across four NetFlow NIDS benchmarks and finds no model generalises across all datasets - the clearest single demonstration of the cross-dataset generalization gap.

title: The Cross-evaluation of Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (XeNIDS)
authors: Giovanni Apruzzese, Luca Pajola, Mauro Conti
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
relevance: First systematic cross-evaluation framework for ML-NIDS over six datasets; shows cross-dataset results collapse relative to in-dataset ones and warns against naive model transfer between networks.

title: Explainable AI for Android Malware Detection: Towards Understanding Why the Models Perform So Well?
relevance: Uses XAI feature attributions to diagnose WHY detectors score high under unrealistic (temporally-inconsistent) settings, connecting explanation analysis to experimental bias and temporal drift.

title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
authors: Daniel Arp, Erwin Quiring, Feargus Pendlebury, Alexander Warnecke, Fabio Pierazzi, Christian Wressnegger, Lorenzo Cavallaro, Konrad Rieck
relevance: Catalogs ten pitfalls of security ML - sampling bias, data snooping, models trained with access to future information, unrealistic class balance - the evaluation-methodology backdrop for all drift claims.

title: 99% False Positives: A Qualitative Study of SOC Analysts' Perspectives on Security Alarms
authors: Bushra A. Alahmadi, Louise Axon, Ivan Martinovic
relevance: Survey (N=20) plus qualitative study (N=21) of SOC practitioners showing most 'false positives' are benign triggers and that alarms must be Reliable, Explainable, Analytical, Contextual, Transferable -- the canonical statement of what analysts actually need from explanation-bearing alerts.
_key: t:99 false positives a qualitative study of soc analysts perspectives on security alarms

title: Explainable AI in Cybersecurity Operations: Lessons Learned from xAI Tool Deployment
authors: Megan Nyre-Yu, Elizabeth S. Morris, Blake Moss, Charles Smutz, Michael R. Smith
relevance: Deployment study of two xAI prototypes with working cyber analysts (Sandia); reports that lack of trust/transparency drives hesitation and distills lessons on fitting explanations into operational workflows -- one of very few real xAI-in-SOC field studies.
_key: t:explainable ai in cybersecurity operations lessons learned from xai tool deployment

title: DeepCASE: Semi-Supervised Contextual Analysis of Security Events
authors: Thijs van Ede, Hojjat Aghakhani, Noah Spahn, Riccardo Bortolameotti, Marco Cova, Andrea Continella, Maarten van Steen, Andreas Peter, Christopher Kruegel, Giovanni Vigna
relevance: Interpretable (attention-based) contextual clustering of security event sequences explicitly designed to cut security operators' manual inspection workload by ~95%; operationalizes 'helping the human' as workload reduction with operator-set policies.

title: TEFL: Turbo Explainable Federated Learning for 6G Trustworthy Zero-Touch Network Slicing
authors: Swastika Roy, Hatim Chergui, Christos Verikoukis
relevance: Closed-loop 'explanation-aware' federated learning for zero-touch slice SLA prediction where Integrated Gradients/SHAP attributions feed a confidence metric constraining training under non-IID data - XAI as an in-the-loop constraint, not post-hoc decoration.

title: An Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection System for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) Attacks
authors: Tahmina Zebin, Shahadate Rezvy, Yuan Luo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (vol. 17, pp. 2339-2349)
relevance: Balanced stacked random forest over the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 dataset detects malicious DoH tunneling with ~99.9% F1, with SHAP values showing per-feature impact on decisions - the reference XAI paper for encrypted-DNS fingerprinting/detection.
_key: t:an explainable ai based intrusion detection system for dns over https doh attacks

title: Evaluating Standard Feature Sets Towards Increased Generalisability and Explainability of ML-based Network Intrusion Detection
authors: M. Sarhan, S. Layeghy, M. Portmann
explanation_method: SHAP feature attributions compared across feature sets
dataset: CSE-CIC-IDS2018, BoT-IoT, ToN-IoT in both NetFlow (NF-*) and CICFlowMeter variants
relevance: Shows the FEATURE SET (NetFlow vs CICFlowMeter) changes both generalisability and explanations - critical for XAI-NTC since traffic classification uses the same two feature families.

title: Evaluating Resilience of Encrypted Traffic Classification Against Adversarial Evasion Attacks
authors: Ramy Maarouf, et al.
relevance: Tests ML and DL encrypted-traffic classifiers against ZOO, PGD and DeepFool evasion, finding DL is generally more resilient than classical ML -- direct traffic-classifier robustness evaluation.

title: Self-attentive deep learning method for online traffic classification and its interpretability (SAM)
authors: Guorui Xie, Qing Li, Yong Jiang
relevance: The clearest instance of attention-weights-as-explanation for traffic: treats initial packet bytes as language, reads self-attention weights as per-byte/header-field importance and cross-checks them against protocol semantics -- but performs no faithfulness test of the Jain-Wallace kind.
_key: t:self attentive deep learning method for online traffic classification and its interpretability sam

title: Assessing a Decision Support Tool for SOC Analysts
authors: Jassim Happa, Ioannis Agrafiotis, Martin Helmhout, Thomas Bashford-Rogers, Michael Goldsmith, Sadie Creese
venue: ACM Digital Threats: Research and Practice (DTRAP)
relevance: Human evaluation of a decision-support/visualization tool with SOC analysts -- a template for measuring whether added machine reasoning actually improves analyst judgments rather than assuming it.

title: Utilizing XAI Technique to Improve Autoencoder based Model for Computer Network Anomaly Detection with Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP)
authors: K. Roshan, A. Zafar
explanation_method: KernelSHAP for feature selection feeding an autoencoder detector
relevance: SHAP-guided feature selection improving an unsupervised detector (94% acc, 0.969 AUC); representative of the XAI-as-feature-engineering pattern.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning under Fire (ADV^2)
authors: Xinyang Zhang, Ningfei Wang, Hua Shen, Shouling Ji, Xiapu Luo, Ting Wang
relevance: First systematic security study of interpretable DL systems; ADV2 crafts inputs that simultaneously fool the classifier and its coupled interpreter, identifying the 'prediction-interpretation gap' as root cause.

title: Black Box Attacks on Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods in Cyber Security
authors: Aditya Kuppa, Nhien-An Le-Khac
relevance: One of the first to attack XAI specifically in the cyber-security setting, showing gradient-based explanations of security classifiers can be manipulated in black-box conditions.

title: Interpreting Deep Learning-Based Networking Systems (Metis)
authors: Zili Meng, Minhu Wang, Jiasong Bai, Mingwei Xu, Hongzi Mao, Hongxin Hu
relevance: Converts DL-based networking controllers into decision trees (local systems) and hypergraphs (global systems) with 'nearly no degradation in performance', demonstrating surrogate distillation as a design/debug/deploy tool for networking DNNs.

title: Enhancing State-of-the-art Classifiers with API Semantics to Detect Evolved Android Malware (APIGraph)
authors: Xiaohan Zhang, Yuan Zhang, Ming Zhong, Daizong Ding, Yinzhi Cao, Yukun Zhang, Mi Zhang, Min Yang
relevance: Shows classifier 'aging' under malware evolution and slows it by encoding API semantic similarity, cutting retraining frequency and labeling effort on a 7-year, 320K-app dataset - the canonical semantic-feature answer to drift.

title: An Assessment of the Usability of Machine Learning Based Tools for the Security Operations Center
authors: Sean Oesch, Robert Bridges, Jared Smith, Justin Beaver, John Goodall, Kelly Huffer, Craig Miles, Dan Scofield
relevance: First in-situ usability study of ML-based detection tools inside operational (Naval) SOCs; documents serious interface violations and analyst mistrust of ML outputs -- direct evidence on whether ML/XAI tooling helps real analysts.

title: Machine Learning Interpretability Meets TLS Fingerprinting
authors: Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Amir Hossein Khajepour, Amirmohammad Ziaei, Amir Ali Gatmiri, Ali Taheri
relevance: Uses ML interpretation techniques to systematically locate the most information-leaking fields of the TLS protocol (handshake, record length, IV) from fingerprinting attacks over 70+ domains - interpretability as a protocol-auditing instrument for encrypted-traffic fingerprinting.

title: Achieving Explainability of Intrusion Detection System by Hybrid Oracle-Explainer Approach
authors: M. Szczepanski, M. Choras, M. Pawlicki, R. Kozik
explanation_method: Surrogate decision tree (oracle-explainer pair: ANN classifier + tree distilled from its outputs, visualized with DtreeViz)
relevance: Early surrogate-model X-IDS; the oracle/explainer split is the simplest deployable alternative to per-decision SHAP.
_key: t:achieving explainability of intrusion detection system by hybrid oracle explainer approach

title: Explanations can be manipulated and geometry is to blame
authors: Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Maximillian Alber, Christopher J. Anders, et al.
relevance: Arbitrarily reshapes explanation maps via imperceptible perturbations that keep outputs fixed, attributing the vulnerability to large network curvature (geometry) and proposing smoothing/soft-plus fixes.

title: Fooling Neural Network Interpretations via Adversarial Model Manipulation
authors: Juyeon Heo, Sunghwan Joo, Taesup Moon
relevance: Attacks the model rather than the input: fine-tunes weights so interpretations (Grad-CAM, LRP) become misleading while accuracy is preserved; fooling transfers across explanation methods.

title: Matched and Mismatched SOCs: A Qualitative Study on Security Operations Center Issues
authors: Faris Bugra Kokulu, Ananta Soneji, Tiffany Bao, Yan Shoshitaishvili, Ziming Zhao, Adam Doupé, Gail-Joon Ahn
relevance: 18 semi-structured interviews with SOC analysts and managers revealing manager/analyst disagreements (including about tool automation and visibility) that any XAI-for-SOC deployment must survive; grounds the 'who is the explanation for' question.

title: EXPLAIN-IT: Towards Explainable AI for Unsupervised Network Traffic Analysis
authors: Andrea Morichetta, Pedro Casas, Marco Mellia
relevance: Brings LIME-style explanations to unsupervised clustering of unlabeled traffic and demonstrates it on YouTube video-quality (QoE) classification under encryption - the earliest dedicated XAI-for-QoE-monitoring methodology.

title: ExplainIt! - A Declarative Root-cause Analysis Engine for Time Series Data
authors: Vimalkumar Jeyakumar, Omid Madani, Ali Parandeh, Ashutosh Kulshreshtha, Weifei Zeng, Navindra Yadav
relevance: Unsupervised, declarative (SQL-like) root-cause analysis engine over datacenter/network telemetry time series from Cisco Tetration, letting operators rank thousands of causal hypotheses - explainable RCA at production scale.

title: IDSGAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Attack Generation against Intrusion Detection
authors: Zilong Lin, Yong Shi, Zhi Xue
relevance: Foundational GAN that transforms malicious flow records into adversarial traffic evading black-box IDS while preserving attack functionality via a restricted-modification mechanism.

title: Transcend: Detecting Concept Drift in Malware Classification Models
authors: Roberto Jordaney, Kumar Sharad, Santanu K. Dash, Zhi Wang, Davide Papini, Ilia Nouretdinov, Lorenzo Cavallaro
relevance: Seminal conformal-evaluation framework that detects concept drift by computing per-class p-values from non-conformity measures instead of trusting classifier confidence, founding the rejection-based drift-detection line all later security-drift work builds on.
_key: t:transcend detecting concept drift in malware classification models

title: Turning Contradictions into Innovations or: How We Learned to Stop Whining and Improve Security Operations
authors: Sathya Chandran Sundaramurthy, John McHugh, Xinming Ou, Michael Wesch, Alexandru G. Bardas, S. Raj Rajagopalan
relevance: 3.5 years of anthropological fieldwork with students embedded as analysts in three SOCs; shows unresolved operational contradictions cause burnout and tool rejection -- context for why analyst-facing explanations succeed or fail.
_key: t:turning contradictions into innovations or how we learned to stop whining and improve security operations

title: TrafficAV: An effective and explainable detection of mobile malware behavior using network traffic
authors: Shanshan Wang, Zhenxiang Chen, et al.
relevance: Early (2016) system explicitly marketed as 'explainable' mobile-malware detection from network traffic, pairing detection with human-meaningful analysis of why an app's traffic is flagged - a seminal precursor of explainable malware-traffic detection.

title: Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks
authors: Robert Geirhos, Joern-Henrik Jacobsen, Claudio Michaelis, Richard Zemel, Wieland Brendel, Matthias Bethge, Felix A. Wichmann
relevance: The concept paper that names and frames 'shortcut learning' (decision rules that pass benchmarks but fail o.o.d.) and recommends interpretation plus o.o.d. testing - the theoretical vocabulary the traffic-classification critique papers all borrow.

title: Towards a Standard Feature Set for Network Intrusion Detection System Datasets
authors: Mohanad Sarhan, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann
relevance: Diagnoses the incomparability of NIDS results caused by each dataset's proprietary feature set and proposes NetFlow-based standard features (NF-CICIDS2017 etc.) to make cross-dataset evaluation possible at all.

title: Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection Systems: LIME and SHAP Applicability on Multi-Layer Perceptron
relevance: Widely cited IDS study validating LIME/SHAP explanations of an MLP via perturbation analysis; representative of how (thinly) explanation validity is checked in most applied NIDS work.

title: Intrusion Detection in the IoT Under Data and Concept Drifts: Online Deep Learning Approach
authors: Omar Abdel Wahab
relevance: Widely-cited online deep learning IDS that explicitly separates data drift from concept drift in IoT streams and adapts online.

title: Evaluating Standard Feature Sets Towards Increased Generalisability and Explainability of ML-based Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Mohanad Sarhan, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann
relevance: Evaluates NetFlow vs CICFlowMeter feature sets across CSE-CIC-IDS2018, BoT-IoT and ToN-IoT and uses SHAP to compare which features drive detection, tying feature-set choice to both generalization and explainability.

title: Inter-dataset generalization strength of supervised machine learning methods for intrusion detection
authors: Laurens D'hooge, Tim Wauters, Bruno Volckaert, Filip De Turck
venue: Journal of Information Security and Applications
relevance: Early systematic evidence that models trained on one CIC-family dataset barely transfer to sibling datasets, foreshadowing the contamination results and challenging claimed generality of ML-IDS.

title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning for Computer Security Applications
authors: Azqa Nadeem, Daniel Vos, Clinton Cao, Luca Pajola, Simon Dieck, Robert Baumgartner, Sicco Verwer
relevance: Systematizes 300 XAI-for-security papers and identifies pitfalls in how explanations are developed and evaluated (e.g., explanations rarely validated with users or ground truth), framing model debugging as the most mature XAI use-case - the XAI-side complement to the dataset-pitfall literature.

title: TrafficFormer: An Efficient Pre-trained Model for Traffic Data
authors: Guangmeng Zhou, Xiongwen Guo, Zhuotao Liu, Tong Li, Qi Li, Ke Xu
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
relevance: State-of-the-art traffic BERT (built on ET-BERT code) adding an SODF pre-training task and field-random-initialization augmentation 'to help the traffic model focus on key information', evaluated on protocol-understanding tasks -- but makes no explainability claim and no attention-faithfulness validation.

title: Model-Based Explanations of Concept Drift
authors: Fabian Hinder, Valerie Vaquet, Johannes Brinkrolf, Barbara Hammer
relevance: General-ML foundation for 'explaining drift': reduces drift explanation to explaining suitably-trained models via spatial feature change - the methodological toolbox NIDS explanation-drift work borrows.

title: I2RNN: An Incremental and Interpretable Recurrent Neural Network for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Zhu Song et al.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
relevance: Interpretable-by-design RNN with sequential fingerprints and local interpretation of per-segment contributions for encrypted traffic -- the strongest non-transformer 'interpretable architecture' baseline in this sub-literature.

title: A Novel Self-Supervised Framework Based on Masked Autoencoder for Traffic Classification
authors: Ruijie Zhao et al.
input_representation: byte matrix (MFR-style) with masked-autoencoder self-supervision
relevance: Journal extension of the YaTC line: MAE self-supervised pre-training over formatted byte matrices for traffic classification, consolidating the masked-reconstruction paradigm on traffic bytes.

title: A Lightweight, Efficient and Explainable-by-Design Convolutional Neural Network for Internet Traffic Classification (LEXNet)
authors: Kevin Fauvel, Fuxing Chen et al.
relevance: Explainable-by-design (prototype-based) traffic classifier; the intrinsic-explanation alternative whose claims still require the evaluation metrics in this corpus to substantiate.

title: Feature Relevance XAI in Anomaly Detection: Reviewing Approaches and Challenges
authors: Julian Tritscher, Anna Krause, Andreas Hotho
relevance: Reviews how feature-relevance XAI is (and mostly is not) evaluated in anomaly detection and argues for ground-truth-bearing synthetic benchmarks, mapping the evaluation gaps for security data.

title: CGNN: Traffic Classification with Graph Neural Network
authors: Bo Pang, Yongquan Fu, Siyuan Ren, Ye Wang, Qing Liao, Yan Jia
input_representation: chained graph over the packet stream (packets as nodes, sequential edges)
relevance: CGNN builds a chained graph over the packet stream and applies a graph classifier for app/malicious/encrypted traffic, arguing packet compositional structure is lost by CNN/RNN models - another graph input representation for explanation methods.

title: In Search of netUnicorn: A Data-Collection Platform to Develop Generalizable ML Models for Network Security Problems
authors: Roman Beltiukov, Wenbo Guo, Arpit Gupta, Walter Willinger
relevance: The constructive follow-up to TRUSTEE: a closed-loop data-collection platform for iteratively removing the inductive biases (shortcuts, o.o.d. fragility) that explanation-based audits reveal in network-security models.

title: TrafficGPT: An LLM Approach for Open-Set Encrypted Traffic Classification
relevance: GPT-2-based feature extraction improves open-set traffic-analysis performance about 12.7% over ET-BERT, representative of the pretrained-transformer wave hitting open-world traffic classification.
authors: Yasod Ginige et al.

title: Additive Feature Attribution Explainable Methods to Craft Adversarial Attacks for Text Classification and Text Regression
authors: Yidong Chai, et al.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE)
relevance: Explanation-guided attack: uses LIME/SHAP token attributions to select high-sensitivity tokens for black-box text adversarial attacks -- same recipe applied to sequence classifiers.

title: Replication: Contrastive Learning and Data Augmentation in Traffic Classification Using a Flowpic Input Representation
authors: Alessandro Finamore et al.
input_representation: flowpic (packet-size/time histogram image) with contrastive augmentation
relevance: Replicates a UCDavis flowpic contrastive-learning result, uncovering dataset problems and smaller-than-reported gains; a rare reproducibility audit of a base representation - evidence for why explanation/validation tooling is needed.

title: AutoML4ETC: Automated Neural Architecture Search for Real-World Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Navid Malekghaini et al.
input_representation: first packet-header bytes of a flow (early classification)
relevance: AutoML4ETC searches neural architectures over early packet-header-byte inputs, beating hand-designed classifiers on real orange-telecom and QUIC traffic; shows the architecture itself is a searchable hyperparameter, complicating model-specific explanations.

title: Many or Few Samples? Comparing Transfer, Contrastive and Meta-Learning in Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Idio Guarino et al.
input_representation: packet-series and payload inputs under transfer/contrastive/meta-learning regimes
relevance: Head-to-head comparison of transfer, meta-, and contrastive learning for label-scarce ETC, finding contrastive representation reuse most effective - maps the label-efficiency axis along which pre-trained base models are chosen.

title: SHAPE: A Simultaneous Header and Payload Encoding Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
input_representation: separate header and payload byte encodings fused simultaneously
relevance: Encodes header and payload bytes as separate views fused for classification under limited labels - early articulation of the header/payload heterogeneity now standard in 2025-2026 pre-trained models.

title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
authors: Maximilian Noppel, Christian Wressnegger
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2024
relevance: Systematizes attacks on explanation methods and their security implications, cautioning that the XAI techniques used to audit traffic classifiers are themselves manipulable - a second-order pitfall for XAI-based NIDS auditing.

title: Robust open-set classification for encrypted traffic fingerprinting
relevance: Open-set treatment of encrypted traffic fingerprinting so classifiers reject flows from classes absent at training.

title: Traffic Generation using Containerization for Machine Learning
authors: Henry Clausen, Robert Flood, David Aspinall
relevance: Diagnoses why lab-generated IDS datasets lack heterogeneity, ground-truth labels, scale and contemporary content, and proposes container-based generation with per-process ground truth as the remedy.

title: Data Augmentation for Traffic Classification
input_representation: packet time-series / flowpic inputs under systematic augmentation study
relevance: Systematically benchmarks augmentation strategies for traffic-classification inputs, showing which invariances actually hold for packet series - defines the perturbation space that perturbation-based XAI methods implicitly assume.

title: AC-DC: Adaptive Ensemble Classification for Network Traffic Identification
authors: Xi Jiang, Shinan Liu, Saloua Naama, Francesco Bronzino, Paul Schmitt, Nick Feamster
relevance: Jiang et al.'s critique-flavored work arguing raw-traffic DL classifiers are too costly and fragile for modern operational settings (companion IETF talk: 'Towards Designing Robust and Efficient Classifiers for Encrypted Traffic in the Modern Internet'); NOTE: an exact 'Jiang et al. reproducibility of DL traffic classification' paper could not be located in arXiv/DBLP/Crossref/S2 - see notes.

title: Reliable Open-Set Network Traffic Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
relevance: RoNeTC quantifies reliability via uncertainty estimation to make open-set traffic classification decisions trustworthy - uncertainty as an implicit form of self-explanation.

title: PacketCLIP: Multi-Modal Embedding of Network Traffic and Language for Cybersecurity Reasoning
authors: Ryozo Masukawa et al.
input_representation: CLIP-style contrastive alignment of packet byte embeddings with natural-language descriptions; hierarchical GNN reasoning
relevance: PacketCLIP contrastively aligns packet content with natural-language semantics for intrusion reasoning - traffic-to-language alignment is a nascent route to natural-language explanations of traffic models.

title: LAMBERT: Leveraging Attention Mechanisms to Improve the BERT Fine-Tuning Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
relevance: Adds a cross-granularity attention fine-tuning head over ET-BERT-style pre-training to fuse packet and byte features -- exemplifies attention added for accuracy with interpretability implied but untested.

title: Facing Unknown: Open-World Encrypted Traffic Classification Based on Contrastive Pre-Training
authors: Xiang Li et al.
input_representation: contrastive pre-training over flows; GAN-synthesized marginal flows for unknown detection
relevance: Open-world ETC via contrastive pre-training plus GAN-based marginal-flow synthesis to detect unknown classes; represents the open-set assumption-relaxation that closed-world base models (and their explanations) usually ignore.

title: OpenCBD: A Network-Encrypted Unknown Traffic Identification Scheme Based on Open-Set Recognition
relevance: Applies open-set recognition (CNN + transformer encoder, three-stage train/test) to flag unknown encrypted traffic classes at inference time.

title: Towards Reproducible Network Traffic Analysis
authors: Jordan Holland, Paul Schmitt, Prateek Mittal, Nick Feamster
relevance: Documents the lack of standardization in traffic-analysis pipelines (representations, splits, tooling) that produces incomparable results, and builds a standard-pipeline framework to enable reproduction.

title: Universal Embedding Function for Traffic Classification via QUIC Domain Recognition Pretraining: A Transfer Learning Success
authors: Jan Luxemburk et al.
input_representation: packet-sequence features of QUIC flows; embedding pre-trained with ArcFace on SNI-domain recognition
relevance: Pre-trains a universal flow-embedding by recognizing QUIC SNI domains with metric learning, then transfers to classification tasks - a non-byte, metadata-sequence route to traffic foundation embeddings.

title: Fooling SHAP with Output Shuffling Attacks
authors: Jun Yuan, et al.
relevance: Introduces data-agnostic output-shuffling attacks that evade Shapley-value bias detection, broadening the catalog of SHAP-specific attacks.

title: Measuring the Complexity of Benchmark NIDS Datasets via Spectral Analysis
authors: Robert Flood, David Aspinall
relevance: Quantifies how 'easy' benchmark NIDS datasets are via spectral complexity measures, explaining why near-perfect scores are achievable and providing a tool to rank dataset difficulty before trusting reported accuracy.

title: Snort Meets Transformers: Accelerating Transformer-Based Network Traffic Classification for Real-Time Performance
relevance: Extracts SHAP attributions from a transformer traffic model and compiles them into Snort signature rules -- explanation used as knowledge-distillation channel from transformer to rule-based IDS.

title: TraGe: A Generic Packet Representation for Traffic Classification Based on Header-Payload Differences
authors: Chungang Lin et al.
input_representation: packet bytes with differentiated header vs. payload masking during pre-training
relevance: TraGe pre-trains with header/payload-differentiated masking, exploiting the fact that header bytes and encrypted payload bytes have fundamentally different statistics - the header-payload heterogeneity theme recurring across 2025-2026 models.

title: ExpMD: an Explainable Framework for Traffic Identification Based on Multi-Domain Features
relevance: Explainable traffic-identification framework that splits network information into four feature domains and attributes decisions to domains -- addresses 'underutilization of information and weak interpretability' in traffic DL.

title: Generic Multi-modal Representation Learning for Network Traffic Analysis
input_representation: multi-modal autoencoder over packet series + payload + flow statistics
relevance: Generic multi-modal representation-learning framework spanning packet series, payload, and flow statistics for multiple traffic-analysis tasks - the modality-fusion direction MIMETIC started, in modern self-supervised form.

title: Few-Shot Open-Set Traffic Classification Based on Self-Supervised Learning
relevance: Combines self-supervised pre-training with unknown-discovery strategies for few-shot open-set encrypted traffic classification.

title: FlowletFormer: Network Behavioral Semantic Aware Pre-training Model for Traffic Classification
authors: Liming Liu et al.
input_representation: protocol-stack-aligned tokenization of packet sequences and flowlets
relevance: FlowletFormer argues generic BERT tokenization ignores network behavioral semantics and aligns tokens/segments with the protocol stack and flowlet structure - directly about making the input representation semantically meaningful (hence explainable).

title: MAWIFlow Benchmark: Realistic Flow-Based Evaluation for Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Joshua Schraven, Alexander Windmann, Oliver Niggemann
relevance: Builds a benchmark from real backbone traffic (MAWILab 2011/2016/2021) specifically because synthetic benchmarks 'fail to reflect statistical variability and temporal drift', and shows tree ensembles degrade sharply across years.

title: MERLOT: A Distilled LLM-based Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Scalable Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Yuxuan Chen et al.
input_representation: contextual feature embeddings of traffic fed to distilled GPT-2 expert models (MoE)
relevance: MERLOT distills GPT-2-based experts into a mixture-of-experts encrypted-traffic classifier for deployment-scale inference; MoE routing adds another layer (which expert fired and why) that explanations must cover.

title: Non-uniformity is All You Need: Efficient and Timely Encrypted Traffic Classification With ECHO
authors: Shilo Daum et al.
input_representation: non-uniform bins of packet sizes and inter-arrival times; early-classification cascade
relevance: ECHO optimizes non-uniform packet-size/timing binning plus an early-classification cascade - shows the size/time input representation itself is tunable, which changes attribution granularity.

title: Explainable Stacking Models based on Complementary Traffic Embeddings
relevance: Stacking meta-learner over complementary traffic embeddings (including transformer embeddings) whose meta-level provides explainability about which embedding type and data source drive each outcome.

title: XAI-Guided Physical Adversarial Machine Learning Attacks on Automatic Modulation Classification
authors: Salmi et al.
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (JSAC)
relevance: Uses SHAP and Grad-CAM++ to guide FGSM-style physical adversarial attacks on RF/modulation classifiers, outperforming non-XAI attacks -- explanation-guided evasion of a signal/traffic classifier.

title: SHLIME: Foiling adversarial attacks fooling SHAP and LIME
authors: Chauhan et al.
relevance: Ensemble defense that restores bias detection under Slack-style scaffolding attacks on SHAP/LIME -- a direct defensive counterpart to the seminal attack.

title: SFA-IoT: segment-to-flow aligned adversarial defense for interpretable IoT device identification
authors: Hussini et al.
relevance: Adversarial purification for interpretable IoT device/traffic identification, restoring accuracy under FGSM/PGD while using SHAP/LIME as diagnostic guidance.

title: NeSySwarm-IDS: End-to-End Differentiable Neuro-Symbolic Logic for Privacy-Preserving Intrusion Detection in UAV Swarms
authors: (MDPI Applied Sciences 16(7):3204)
relevance: End-to-end differentiable neuro-symbolic logic IDS with built-in interpretability under UAV-swarm resource and privacy constraints -- differentiable-logic explanation-by-design at the network edge.

title: Neuro-symbolic machine learning for lightweight and interpretable IoT edge intrusion detection
authors: (Discover Sensors, 2026; see article page)
relevance: Lightweight neuro-symbolic IDS for IoT edge devices where the symbolic component supplies interpretability at low compute -- the efficiency argument for symbolic explanations in NIDS.

title: DQSA: Dynamic Quantized Self-Attention for Multi-Task Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
relevance: Argues different tasks attend to distinct regions of the traffic sequence and proposes dynamic, interpretable attention for multi-task classification -- attention interpretability claimed as a design property, again unvalidated against faithfulness criteria.

title: Session Aware Encrypted Traffic Classification with Contextual Position Selection
relevance: One of the only traffic papers to state the attention-explanation problem outright -- prior methods 'rely on attention mechanisms with unstable scores and hard interpretation, posing risks in security-critical scenarios' -- and to design an alternative position-selection mechanism because of it.

title: Empirical Analysis of Evasion and Poisoning Against Malware Data Drift Detection
relevance: Attacks drift detectors themselves (evasion and poisoning), showing drift-detection components add a distinct attack surface - relevant to trusting drift explanations.

title: Nethira: A Heterogeneity-aware Hierarchical Pre-trained Model for Network Traffic Classification
authors: Chungang Lin et al.
input_representation: hierarchical byte / protocol-field / packet-level reconstruction over raw sequences
relevance: Nethira (2026) pre-trains with hierarchical reconstruction spanning byte, protocol, and packet levels of raw traffic - the current frontier of heterogeneity-aware traffic pre-training.

title: MambaNetBurst: Direct Byte-level Network Traffic Classification without Tokenization or Pretraining
authors: Gayan K. Kulatilleke et al.
input_representation: fixed-length raw-byte bursts from the first few packets, Mamba-2 backbone, no tokenizer
relevance: MambaNetBurst classifies fixed-length raw-byte bursts with a Mamba-2 backbone and no tokenization or pre-training, challenging the assumption that traffic needs BERT-style pipelines at all - a counterpoint model for explanation studies.

title: UniAlign: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Robust Network Traffic Classification under Distribution Shifts
input_representation: model-agnostic alignment layer over existing classifiers' representations
relevance: Model-agnostic robustness wrapper aligning representations of existing traffic classifiers under distribution shift - part of the robustness wave (with Rosetta, FG-SAT) responding to fragile learned features.

title: PERO: Efficient Robust Post-Training Foundation Models for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Wumei Du et al.
input_representation: post-training of byte-sequence traffic foundation models with sample-wise risk proxy
relevance: PERO post-trains encrypted-traffic foundation models for robustness using a lightweight sample-risk proxy - 2026 evidence that FM fragility is now treated as a first-class problem.

title: Where Do Flow Semantics Reside? A Protocol-Native Tabular Pretraining Paradigm for Encrypted Traffic Classification (FlowSem-MAE)
authors: Sizhe Huang et al.
input_representation: tabular masked autoencoder over protocol-defined field units (Flow Semantic Units), not raw byte streams
relevance: Asks the representation question head-on ('where do flow semantics reside?') and pre-trains a tabular MAE over protocol-defined field units instead of undifferentiated bytes - protocol-native inputs make attributions land on named fields.

title: NetMamba+: A Framework of Pre-trained Models for Efficient and Accurate Network Traffic Classification
authors: Tongze Wang et al.
input_representation: multimodal byte-preserving traffic representation over Mamba backbone
relevance: NetMamba+ extends the Mamba pre-trained-classifier line with a multimodal byte-preserving representation - current frontier of the efficiency-oriented SSM family.

title: TrafficMoE: Heterogeneity-aware Mixture of Experts for Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Qing He et al.
input_representation: disentangled header and payload streams routed to sparse experts with uncertainty-aware filtering
relevance: TrafficMoE routes disentangled header vs. payload representations through sparse experts - the MoE + header/payload-heterogeneity synthesis closing out the 2026 model wave.

title: Decision-Aware Trust Signal Alignment for SOC Alert Triage
authors: Israt Jahan Chowdhury, Md Abu Yousuf Tanvir
relevance: Simulation study (LR/RF on UNSW-NB15) showing misaligned confidence/uncertainty displays amplify costly triage errors; a decision-theoretic account of trust signals -- but no human subjects, so its interface claims await user-study validation.

title: Lost in Translation: Intrusion Detection Research with 'Kaggle Datasets'
authors: Jukka Ruohonen
relevance: Critiques the secondary-distribution problem: IDS papers increasingly train on re-hosted 'Kaggle' copies of benchmark datasets with undocumented provenance and modifications, compounding label-error and reproducibility issues.

title: Explainable Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic Using Normalizing Flows
authors: (per DBLP listing)
explanation_method: Normalizing-flow density model with per-feature likelihood decomposition as explanation
relevance: Density-based explainable anomaly detection in a top networking venue - probabilistic alternative to attribution methods.

title: Explainable Visual Anomaly Detection via Concept Bottleneck Models
relevance: Extends concept bottleneck models to (visual) anomaly detection -- evidence CBMs are spreading to anomaly-detection settings, while network-traffic CBMs remain nonexistent.

title: On the Consistency of GNN Explanations for Malware Detection
authors: Hossein Shokouhinejad et al.
relevance: Evaluates GNNExplainer, PGExplainer and CaptumExplainer for stability/consistency on control-flow-graph malware detection and proposes RankFusion aggregation -- the explanation-quality methodology GNN-NIDS work lacks, in a sibling security domain.

title: Exploring the Potential and Boundaries of KAN in Encrypted Traffic Classification
authors: Shituo Ma et al.
relevance: Replaces MLP blocks with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for 'end-to-end interpretable encrypted traffic classification' via spline-function visualization -- the interpretable-architecture-swap answer to the same opacity complaint ('traditional deep learning-based encrypted traffic classification models generally suffer from weak interpretability').

title: Empirical Evaluation of Concept Drift in ML-Based Android Malware Detection
relevance: Cross-algorithm drift study (nine ML/DL algorithms plus LLMs) finding drift is widespread and that few-shot LLMs do not fully mitigate it.

title: "Explain, Don't Just Warn!" -- A Real-Time Framework for Generating Phishing Warnings with Contextual Explanations
authors: Sayak Saha Roy, Cesar Torres, Shirin Nilizadeh
relevance: User study (N=150) showing explainable real-time phishing warnings beat generic ones on understanding and threat-identification accuracy -- explanation helping end users in a security task, with the real-time generation constraint made explicit.

title: Explainable AI in Usable Privacy and Security: Challenges and Opportunities
authors: Vincent Freiberger, Arthur Fleig, Erik Buchmann
relevance: N=22 user study of LLM-generated explanations in privacy-policy assessment; surfaces transparency/consistency/faithfulness concerns with LLM judges and argues for adaptive explanation strategies in security-adjacent settings.

title: eX-NIDS: A Framework for Explainable Network Intrusion Detection Leveraging Large Language Models
authors: P. R. B. Houssel, S. Layeghy, P. Singh, M. Portmann
explanation_method: LLM explanations of flagged malicious flows enriched with CTI context; evaluated against baseline prompting
relevance: Journal-version LLM-explanation framework for NIDS flows from the same group as the negative-result study.

title: LENS-XAI: Redefining Lightweight and Explainable Network Security through Knowledge Distillation and Variational Autoencoders
authors: (authors per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Attribution-based explainability on a knowledge-distilled VAE student
relevance: Explainability under edge resource constraints via distillation - the deployment-cost thread.

title: XAInomaly: Explainable and Interpretable Deep Contractive Autoencoder for O-RAN Traffic Anomaly Detection
authors: O. T. Basaran, F. Dressler
explanation_method: fastSHAP-C real-time approximation over a deep contractive autoencoder
relevance: Real-time SHAP approximation for streaming telecom traffic - latency-aware XAI, the operational constraint NTC shares.

title: Explainable Network Anomaly Detection with GraphSAGE and SHAP
authors: (per DBLP listing)
explanation_method: SHAP over GraphSAGE node embeddings
relevance: SHAP applied to graph representation of traffic - method/representation combination relevant to GNN-NTC.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Cyberattack Identification from Traffic Flows
authors: (authors per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Deep learning + XAI on simulated traffic-light-network flows
relevance: Flow-level attack identification with explanations; documents stealth-attack blind spots.

title: L-XAIDS: A LIME-based eXplainable AI framework for Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: (authors per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: LIME + ELI5 local/global explanations with decision-tree support
relevance: LIME-centric counterpart to the SHAP-dominant literature.

title: A Novel Perturb-ability Score to Mitigate Evasion Adversarial Attacks on Flow-Based ML-NIDS
authors: Mohamed elShehaby, Ashraf Matrawy
relevance: Defines a per-feature 'perturb-ability' score to identify which flow features an attacker can realistically manipulate, using it to harden flow-based NIDS -- feature-realism defense.

title: Towards Explainable Network Intrusion Detection using Large Language Models
authors: Paul R. B. Houssel, Priyanka Singh, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann
relevance: Precursor study benchmarking LLMs as NIDS explainers (and finding them unfit as detectors but promising as explanation generators) -- baseline for the natural-language explanation thread.

title: Explainable Malware Detection with Tailored Logic Explained Networks
authors: Peter Anthony, Francesco Giannini, Michelangelo Diligenti, Martin Homola, Marco Gori, Stefan Balogh, Jan Mojzis
relevance: Adapts Logic Explained Networks (FOL-rule self-explaining nets) to EMBER malware detection with robustness rivaling black boxes -- the closest LEN deployment to networking; LENs remain untried on traffic flows.

title: Explainable Malware Detection through Integrated Graph Reduction and Learning Techniques
authors: Hesamodin Mohammadian et al.
relevance: Combines graph-reduction with GNNExplainer on control/function-call graphs, showing explanation quality survives graph compression -- relevant to scaling GNN explanations to large traffic graphs.

title: MORPH: Towards Automated Concept Drift Adaptation for Malware Detection
relevance: Pseudo-label self-training for neural malware detectors that reduces annotation effort under drift when combined with active learning.

title: Seamless Website Fingerprinting in Multiple Environments
relevance: Shows website-fingerprinting CNNs lose accuracy when training lacks network-location/client variability and applies domain adaptation to generalize across environments.

title: One Train for Two Tasks: An Encrypted Traffic Classification Framework Using Supervised Contrastive Learning (CLE-TFE)
authors: Haozhen Zhang et al.
input_representation: byte-level traffic graphs with graph augmentation; joint packet-level and flow-level tasks
relevance: Applies supervised contrastive learning and graph augmentation on byte-level traffic graphs, classifying packet and flow levels in one training run; representative of contrastive refinements to the byte-graph representation.

title: FG-SAT: Efficient Flow Graph for Encrypted Traffic Classification under Environment Shifts
authors: Susu Cui et al.
input_representation: flow graph of internal flow relationships; feature selection via Jensen-Shannon divergence
relevance: Represents flows as graphs of internal relationships with divergence-based feature selection to survive environment shifts - graph-input robustness work motivated by the same deployment fragility XAI aims to diagnose.

title: AI-Driven Guided Response for Security Operation Centers with Microsoft Copilot for Security (GUIDE dataset)
authors: Scott Freitas, Jovan Kalajdjieski, Amir Gharib, Rob McCann
relevance: Guided-response recommendation at SOC scale plus release of GUIDE: ~1M incidents with customer-analyst annotations -- currently the largest public resource for human-grounded evaluation of SOC assistance.

title: Robust and Reliable Early-Stage Website Fingerprinting Attacks via Spatial-Temporal Distribution Analysis (Holmes)
authors: Xinhao Deng, Xiyuan Zhao, Qilei Yin, Zhuotao Liu, Qi Li, Mingwei Xu, Ke Xu, Jianping Wu
relevance: State-of-the-art early-stage website fingerprinting whose design is driven by feature-attribution (SHAP-style importance of traffic features per page-loading stage); identifies dark-web sites at ~21.7% page load with +169% F1 over nine DL attacks - interpretability used to engineer the attack.

title: X-CANIDS: Signal-Aware Explainable Intrusion Detection System for Controller Area Network-Based In-Vehicle Network
authors: S. Jeong, S. Lee, H. Lee, H. K. Kim
explanation_method: Signal-level attribution from autoencoder reconstruction errors on deserialized CAN signals
relevance: Shows feature-level explainability engineered INTO the detector for streaming in-vehicle traffic.

title: Explainable AI for Comparative Analysis of Intrusion Detection Models
authors: P. Wickramasinghe et al. (per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Occlusion sensitivity across RF, SVM, KNN, decision trees, MLP
relevance: Cross-model attribution comparison concluding feature engineering beats model complexity for IDS.

title: An Adversarial Approach: Explainable and Transferable Adversarial Attack for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detectors
authors: H. He et al. (per arXiv listing; ETA framework)
explanation_method: Cooperative-game (Shapley-style) interpretation of adversarial perturbations to explain attack transferability
relevance: XAI used by the ATTACKER: explains which features make NIDS evasion transfer - the adversarial mirror of SHAP-for-defense.

title: Bridging the Gap: Advancing the Transparency and Trustworthiness of Network Intrusion Detection with Explainable AI
authors: (per Springer listing)
venue: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
explanation_method: SHAP/LIME-based transparency framework for NIDS
relevance: Journal-length treatment of trustworthiness framing for XAI-NIDS.

title: An Interpretable Generalization Mechanism for Accurately Detecting Anomaly and Identifying Networking Intrusion Techniques
authors: H.-C. Yang et al. (per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Interpretable pattern-based generalization (rule/pattern matching between normal and attack profiles)
relevance: Inherently-interpretable generalization mechanism evaluated across three flow datasets.

title: Transforming In-Vehicle Network Intrusion Detection: VAE-based Knowledge Distillation Meets Explainable AI
authors: M. Nazari et al. (per arXiv listing; KD-XVAE)
explanation_method: SHAP over a VAE-distilled lightweight student model
relevance: Explainability retained through model compression - relevant to any edge-deployed traffic model.

title: Review on the Feasibility of Adversarial Evasion Attacks and Defenses for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Islam Debicha, Benjamin Cochez, Tayeb Kenaza, Thibault Debatty, Jean-Michel Dricot, Wim Mees
relevance: Survey of the feasibility of evasion attacks/defenses specific to NIDS; good background hub for the adversarial-traffic half of the angle.

title: TAD: Transfer learning-based multi-adversarial detection of evasion attacks against network intrusion detection systems
authors: Islam Debicha, Richard Bauwens, Thibault Debatty, Jean-Michel Dricot, Tayeb Kenaza, Wim Mees
relevance: Defense that stacks multiple transfer-learned detectors to catch adversarial evasion traffic against NIDS.

title: Robust Explanation Constraints for Neural Networks
authors: Matthew Wicker, Juyeon Heo, Luca Costabello, Adrian Weller
relevance: Trains networks with certified constraints so gradient explanations provably cannot be moved outside a set by bounded perturbations -- explanation-robustness certification.
_key: t:robust explanation constraints for neural networks

title: Fooling SHAP with Stealthily Biased Sampling
authors: Gabriel Laberge, Ulrich Aivodji, Satoshi Hara, Mario Marchand, Foutse Khomh
relevance: Manipulates SHAP global explanations by biasing the background sampling distribution rather than the model -- a data-side attack on Shapley explanations.
_key: t:fooling shap with stealthily biased sampling

title: Foiling Explanations in Deep Neural Networks
authors: Snir Vitrack Tamam, Raz Lapid, Moshe Sipper
relevance: AttaXAI: a black-box, query-only evolution-strategy attack that manipulates image explanations without model access -- shows attacks work without gradients.

title: Explaining AI-Informed Network Intrusion Detection with Counterfactuals
authors: Meng Jiang group (Notre Dame; demo/poster paper)
relevance: Early demo system visualizing counterfactual examples (t-SNE plus minimal feature flips) for NID datasets -- evidence that counterfactual-for-NIDS work started as small demos before the 2025 full frameworks.
