title: A Dual-Perspective Approach to Evaluating Feature Attribution Methods
authors: Yawei Li et al.
relevance: Splits faithfulness into soundness and completeness with corresponding metrics, addressing shortcomings the authors identify in existing faithfulness evaluations.

title: AttributionLab: Faithfulness of Feature Attribution Under Controllable Environments
authors: Yang Zhang et al.
relevance: Manually designs network weights so ground-truth attribution is known exactly; a fully controlled sanity-testing environment for attribution methods.

title: Manipulation Risks in Explainable AI: The Implications of the Disagreement Problem
authors: Sofie Goethals, David Martens, Theodoros Evgeniou
relevance: Argues that because explainers disagree, providers can cherry-pick explanations (fairwashing risk), giving an adversarial/security reading of the disagreement problem.

title: That Escalated Quickly: An ML Framework for Alert Prioritization
authors: Ben Gelman, Salma Taoufiq, Tamás Vörös, Konstantin Berlin
relevance: Production alert-prioritization system measured in analyst-relevant units (22.9% faster response, 54% FP suppression); the workload-metrics counterpoint to explanation-centric help for SOC humans.

title: Efficient Shapley Values Estimation by Amortization for Text Classification
authors: Chenghao Yang, Fan Yin, He He, Kai-Wei Chang, Xiaofei Ma, Bing Xiang
relevance: Amortized Shapley estimator (up to 60x speedup) that also exposes the instability of sampling-based Shapley under limited budgets -- speed and explanation stability trade off, a caution for real-time security attribution.

title: Explainable AI in 6G O-RAN: A Tutorial and Survey on Architecture, Use Cases, Challenges, and Future Research
authors: Bouziane Brik, Hatim Chergui, Lanfranco Zanzi, Francesco Devoti, Adlen Ksentini, Muhammad Shuaib Siddiqui, Xavier Costa-Perez, Christos Verikoukis
venue: arXiv tutorial/survey (IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials version exists)
relevance: Tutorial-survey on deploying XAI inside O-RAN RIC control loops (xApps/rApps), covering automated XAI pipelines and security of explanations - the most operationally concrete of the 6G XAI surveys.

title: Using Kernel SHAP XAI Method to Optimize the Network Anomaly Detection Model
authors: K. Roshan, A. Zafar
explanation_method: KernelSHAP global rankings to prune features
relevance: Follow-up quantifying detection gains from SHAP-selected features in unsupervised mode.

title: SoK: Modeling Explainability in Security Analytics for Interpretability, Trustworthiness, and Usability
authors: D. Mink et al.
explanation_method: SoK comparing XAI methods on security analytics tasks incl. anomaly detection; studies adversarial manipulation of explanations
relevance: Highlights that explanation methods themselves are attackable - a robustness dimension XAI-NTC must inherit.

title: Explainable Intrusion Detection Systems Using Competitive Learning Techniques
authors: J. Ables, T. Kirby, S. Mittal, S. Rahimi, I. Banicescu, M. Seale
explanation_method: SOM/GSOM/GHSOM white-box competitive learning with visual explanations
relevance: Quantifies the accuracy cost of inherent interpretability (1-3% below black-box ensembles).

title: Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection in the Internet of Things
authors: M. Siganos, P. Radoglou-Grammatikis, I. Kotsiuba, E. Markakis, I. Moscholios, S. Goudos, P. Sarigiannidis
explanation_method: SHAP/LIME over ML/DL detectors for IoT
relevance: Representative ACM-venue applied XAI-IDS for IoT with open-access PDF.

title: Comprehensive Analysis Over Centralized and Federated Learning-Based Anomaly Detection in Networks with Explainable AI (XAI)
authors: (per DBLP listing)
explanation_method: SHAP-style XAI compared across centralized vs federated anomaly detectors
relevance: Explains how federation changes both accuracy and explanations for network anomaly detection.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning based Evasion Generative Adversarial Network for Botnet Detection
authors: Rizwan Hamid Randhawa, et al.
relevance: Combines DRL with a GAN to generate semantics-preserving evasion traffic against botnet detectors, converging faster within functional constraints.

title: Certifiably robust interpretation via Renyi differential privacy
authors: Ao Liu, Xiaoyu Chen, Sijia Liu, Lirong Xia, Chuang Gan
relevance: Provides certified robustness guarantees for feature-attribution explanations using Renyi differential privacy -- the certification angle for explanation robustness.

title: Is your explanation stable? A Robustness Evaluation Framework for Feature Attribution
authors: Yuyou Gan, Yuhao Mao, Xuhong Zhang, Shouling Ji, et al.
relevance: Proposes Median Test for Feature Attribution to statistically evaluate whether an explanation is stable under adversarial perturbation -- a robustness-evaluation methodology.

title: Fooling Partial Dependence via Data Poisoning
authors: Hubert Baniecki, Wojciech Kretowicz, Przemyslaw Biecek
relevance: Poisons data to arbitrarily bend Partial Dependence Plots using genetic and gradient algorithms -- extends explanation manipulation to global model-agnostic explanations.

title: EBSNN: Extended Byte Segment Neural Network for Network Traffic Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing 19(5)
relevance: Pre-transformer byte-segment RNN with attention over header/payload segments -- the earlier attention-over-bytes lineage whose attention weights were likewise presented as indicating discriminative segments.
_key: t:ebsnn extended byte segment neural network for network traffic classification

title: Fast & Furious: Modelling Malware Detection as Evolving Data Streams
relevance: Stream-learning view of malware detection over nine years of data; notably updates the FEATURE EXTRACTOR as well as the classifier when drift is signaled.

title: "Is Your Explanation Stable?": A Robustness Evaluation Framework for Feature Attribution
authors: Yuyou Gan et al.
relevance: MeTFA gives statistically guaranteed stability intervals for attributions under noise; a security-oriented treatment of explanation-stability measurement.

title: A Multilingual Perspective Towards the Evaluation of Attribution Methods in Natural Language Inference
authors: Kerem Zaman, Yonatan Belinkov
relevance: Builds faithfulness measurement on cross-lingual word alignments to avoid erasure drawbacks; an example of designing domain-appropriate substitutes for deletion metrics.

title: Mousika: Enable General In-Network Intelligence in Programmable Switches by Knowledge Distillation
authors: Guorui Xie, Qing Li, Yutao Dong, Guanglin Duan, Yong Jiang, Jingpu Duan
relevance: Distills black-box models into binary decision trees encoded as ternary match rules that run at line rate in programmable switches -- the deployment-side answer to explanation cost: make the deployed model itself transparent and per-packet cheap.

title: Accelerating Shapley Explanation via Contributive Cooperator Selection (SHEAR)
authors: Guanchu Wang, Yu-Neng Chuang, Mengnan Du, Fan Yang, Quan Zhou, Pushkar Tripathi, Xuanting Cai, Xia Hu
relevance: Cuts Shapley cost by evaluating only selected feature coalitions via a Shapley chain rule; representative of the coalition-pruning family of speedups relevant to low-latency attribution.

title: WindowSHAP: An Efficient Framework for Explaining Time-series Classifiers based on Shapley Values
authors: Amin Nayebi, Sindhu Tipirneni, Chandan K. Reddy, Brandon Foreman, Vignesh Subbian
relevance: Windowed Shapley attribution cutting KernelSHAP CPU time ~80% on long sequences -- directly transferable to packet/flow sequence models where per-timestep SHAP is unaffordable.

title: Creating an Explainable Intrusion Detection System Using Self Organizing Maps
authors: J. Ables, T. Kirby, W. Anderson, S. Mittal, S. Rahimi, I. Banicescu, M. Seale
explanation_method: Self-Organizing Maps as inherently-interpretable classifier (U-matrix, feature heatmaps for global; BMU analysis for local)
relevance: White-box-by-construction alternative to post-hoc XAI for flow features.

title: An Interpretable Federated Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Framework
authors: T. Zebin et al. (per arXiv listing; FEDFOREST)
explanation_method: Interpretable-by-design GBDT combined with federated learning
relevance: Interpretable trees under federation - privacy-preserving deployments where post-hoc XAI is hardest.

title: Counterfactual Explanations Can Be Manipulated
authors: Dylan Slack, Sophie Hilgard, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Sameer Singh
relevance: Extends explanation-manipulation to counterfactual/recourse explanations, showing models can be built to give unfairly cheap recourse to chosen subgroups.

title: Investigating Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps with Image and Text Classification
authors: Narine Kokhlikyan et al.
relevance: Replicates sanity checks across modalities and shows conclusions depend on modality, baselines and smoothness, i.e. randomization-test outcomes are configuration-sensitive.

title: Considerations for Deploying xAI Tools in the Wild: Lessons Learned from xAI Deployment in a Cybersecurity Operations Setting
authors: Megan Nyre-Yu, Michael R. Smith, et al.
relevance: Companion workshop paper to the USEC study; practical considerations (integration, analyst time budgets, explanation consumption) for deploying xAI tools in operational security settings.
_key: t:considerations for deploying xai tools in the wild lessons learned from xai deployment in a cybersecurity operations setting

title: FastSHAP: Real-Time Shapley Value Estimation
authors: Neil Jethani, Mukund Sudarshan, Ian Covert, Su-In Lee, Rajesh Ranganath
relevance: Amortized learned explainer producing Shapley estimates in a single forward pass with orders-of-magnitude speedup -- the reference point for making per-flow SHAP feasible at inference time.

title: Fast TreeSHAP: Accelerating SHAP Value Computation for Trees
authors: Jilei Yang
relevance: CPU-side TreeSHAP variants (v1 1.5x, v2 2.5-3x faster via precomputation) for industry-scale batch explanation -- the trade of memory for explanation latency.

title: Applications of Explainable AI for 6G: Technical Aspects, Use Cases, and Research Challenges
authors: Shen Wang, M. Atif Qureshi, Luis Miralles-Pechuan, Thien Huynh-The, Thippa Reddy Gadekallu, Madhusanka Liyanage
relevance: Survey mapping XAI methods onto 6G technical enablers including intelligent radio and zero-touch network management, cataloguing use cases and open challenges - orientation map for the whole XAI-for-networking space.

title: New Directions in Automated Traffic Analysis (nPrint/nPrintML)
authors: Jordan Holland, Paul Schmitt, Nick Feamster, Prateek Mittal
relevance: Standard bit-level packet representation plus AutoML across eight traffic-analysis tasks (device identification among them); its uniform representation makes feature-importance analysis comparable across tasks and it is the model family Trustee later audited - key infrastructure hub.

title: Defending network intrusion detection systems against adversarial evasion attacks
authors: Marek Pawlicki, Michal Choras, Rafal Kozik
relevance: Early defense study detecting adversarial evasion at NIDS inference time; frequently cited baseline for the adversarial-NIDS thread.

title: Fairwashing Explanations with Off-Manifold Detergent
authors: Christopher J. Anders, Plamen Pasliev, Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Klaus-Robert Muller, Pan Kessel
relevance: Demonstrates two same-accuracy classifiers can be made to yield arbitrary (fairwashed) explanations by exploiting off-manifold behavior; proposes a manifold-based robustness fix.

title: Smoothed Geometry for Robust Attribution
authors: Zifan Wang, Haofan Wang, Shakul Ramkumar, Matt Fredrikson, Piotr Mardziel, Anupam Datta
relevance: Derives Lipschitz/geometry conditions under which gradient attributions are robust and regularizes for them; complements Dombrowski's geometry diagnosis with a defense.

title: Interpretable Sequence Classification via Discrete Optimization
authors: Maayan Shvo, Andrew C. Li, Rodrigo Toro Icarte, Sheila A. McIlraith
relevance: Learns finite-state-automata classifiers via MILP for early sequence classification (intrusion-detection motivated), supporting explanation, counterfactual reasoning and human-in-the-loop edits -- automata as an interpretable-by-design alternative for sequential traffic, never applied to real packet/flow traces.

title: Counterfactual Explanations of Concept Drift
authors: Fabian Hinder, Barbara Hammer
relevance: First formulation of explaining drift itself in human-understandable counterfactual terms, ancestor of the causal drift-explanation line.

title: GPUTreeShap: Massively Parallel Exact Calculation of SHAP Scores for Tree Ensembles
authors: Rory Mitchell, Eibe Frank, Geoffrey Holmes
relevance: Exact TreeSHAP on GPUs: up to 19x (values) / 340x (interactions) speedups and ~1.2M rows/sec throughput -- concrete numbers for what SHAP-at-scale costs on the tree ensembles common in flow-feature traffic classifiers.

title: Improving KernelSHAP: Practical Shapley Value Estimation via Linear Regression
authors: Ian Covert, Su-In Lee
relevance: Variance analysis and convergence acceleration for model-agnostic KernelSHAP, incl. uncertainty estimates that tell you when to stop sampling -- governs the samples-vs-latency dial any online NIDS explainer must set.

title: Robust Attribution Regularization
authors: Jiefeng Chen, Xi Wu, Vaibhav Rastogi, Yingyu Liang, Somesh Jha
relevance: Training objective that makes Integrated Gradients attributions robust to input perturbation; a canonical defense against attribution attacks.

title: Inferring Streaming Video Quality from Encrypted Traffic: Practical Models and Deployment Experience
authors: Francesco Bronzino, Paul Schmitt, Sara Ayoubi, Guilherme Martins, Renata Teixeira, Nick Feamster
venue: Proc. ACM on Measurement and Analysis of Computing Systems / SIGMETRICS 2020
relevance: Deployment-grade interpretable-feature models inferring startup delay and resolution for Netflix/YouTube/Amazon/Twitch from encrypted traffic across 66 homes for 16 months; feature-composition analysis (which layers of features matter) is the interpretability contribution for QoE inference.

title: ACE - An Anomaly Contribution Explainer for Cyber-Security Applications
authors: X. Zhang, M. Marwah, I-T. Lee, M. Arlitt, D. Goldwasser
explanation_method: Local linear-regression surrogate producing per-feature contribution scores for black-box anomaly scores (+ ACE-KL variant)
dataset: CERT insider threat, NetFlow, Android malware
relevance: Early general-purpose anomaly-score explainer evaluated on netflow - predecessor of SHAP-for-anomaly pipelines.

title: Domain Knowledge Aided Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Intrusion Detection and Response
authors: S. R. Islam, W. Eberle, S. K. Ghafoor, A. Siraj, M. Rogers
explanation_method: CIA-principle (domain knowledge) infused feature grouping for interpretable IDS
relevance: Early argument that security-domain semantics, not generic attributions, make IDS explanations meaningful.

title: The Challenge of Detecting Sophisticated Attacks: Insights from SOC Analysts
authors: Olusola Akinrolabu, Ioannis Agrafiotis, Arnau Erola
relevance: Interview-based study of SOC analysts on detecting sophisticated attacks; early evidence of the tooling/insight gaps that analyst-facing explanation systems claim to fill.

title: Measuring Information Leakage in Website Fingerprinting Attacks and Defenses (WeFDE)
authors: Shuai Li, Huajun Guo, Nicholas Hopper
relevance: Information-theoretic framework quantifying mutual information leaked by all 3,043 features from the Tor WF literature over 211,219 visits - the feature-level 'ground truth of importance' against which model-level WF explanations are judged.

title: A machine learning approach to classifying YouTube QoE based on encrypted network traffic
authors: Irena Orsolic, Dario Pevec, Mirko Suznjevic, Lea Skorin-Kapov
relevance: Operator-side YouTube QoE classification from encrypted traffic with explicit feature analysis of which traffic-level features carry QoE information - foundational interpretable-ML line for in-network QoE monitoring.

title: Taking the Blame Game out of Data Centers Operations with NetPoirot
authors: Behnaz Arzani, Selim Ciraci, Boon Thau Loo, Assaf Schuster, Geoff Outhred
relevance: Decision-tree-based fault blame allocation (client vs network vs remote) from endpoint TCP statistics with ~96% accuracy for some failure types - the classic interpretable-by-design root-cause-analysis system predating the XAI wave.

title: A Human Capital Model for Mitigating Security Analyst Burnout
authors: Sathya Chandran Sundaramurthy, Alexandru G. Bardas, Jacob Case, Xinming Ou, Michael Wesch, John McHugh, S. Raj Rajagopalan
relevance: Ethnography-derived model of analyst burnout as cyclic interaction of human, technical, and managerial factors; motivates workload-reducing (not just transparency-adding) uses of XAI in SOCs.
_key: t:a human capital model for mitigating security analyst burnout

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI): Concepts, Taxonomies, Opportunities and Challenges toward Responsible AI
authors: A. Barredo Arrieta, N. Diaz-Rodriguez, J. Del Ser, et al.
explanation_method: General XAI taxonomy (transparency levels, post-hoc families)
relevance: The general-XAI taxonomy nearly every XAI-NIDS/NTC paper uses to classify its method; citation count retrieved via Crossref.

title: Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning
authors: Finale Doshi-Velez, Been Kim
relevance: The application-grounded / human-grounded / functionally-grounded evaluation taxonomy nearly every XAI-evaluation paper builds on; notes 'very little consensus on what interpretable machine learning is and how it should be measured'.

title: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
authors: Rex Ying et al.
relevance: Canonical post-hoc GNN explainer (mutual-information-maximal subgraph + feature mask); the method most frequently borrowed by GNN-based NIDS/botnet papers to claim explainability.

title: Attention is not Explanation
authors: Sarthak Jain, Byron C. Wallace
relevance: Foundational negative result: attention weights correlate weakly with gradient-based importance and admit adversarial distributions yielding identical predictions -- the benchmark any 'attention heatmap = explanation' claim in traffic transformers must answer.

title: Quantifying Attention Flow in Transformers
authors: Samira Abnar, Willem H. Zuidema
relevance: Attention rollout/flow: raw per-layer attention is unreliable in deep transformers because information mixes across layers; directly undermines single-layer attention heatmaps of the kind shown for 12-layer traffic BERTs.

title: Attention is not not Explanation
authors: Sarah Wiegreffe, Yuval Pinter
relevance: Rebuttal defining testing protocols (uniform-weights baseline, variance calibration, adversarial training of attention) for when attention can serve as explanation; supplies the exact experimental designs a traffic-transformer validation study would need.

title: Transformer Interpretability Beyond Attention Visualization
authors: Hila Chefer, Shir Gur, Lior Wolf
relevance: LRP-based relevance propagation through self-attention as a principled alternative to raw attention maps; the natural candidate method for ViT-style traffic models (YaTC's MFR-matrix ViT) that nobody has yet applied to traffic.

title: Kitsune: An Ensemble of Autoencoders for Online Network Intrusion Detection
authors: Y. Mirsky, T. Doitshman, Y. Elovici, A. Shabtai
explanation_method: None (baseline system) - included because it is the standard subject model that DeepAID and TRUSTEE explain
dataset: Kitsune dataset (Mirai and 8 other attacks), released with paper
relevance: The unsupervised NIDS whose feature mapper (AfterImage incremental statistics) and dataset became the de-facto testbed for anomaly-detection explainability work.

title: Is Attention Interpretable?
authors: Sofia Serrano, Noah A. Smith
relevance: Intervention study (zeroing attended representations) showing attention weights only partially indicate importance -- the third leg of the debate canon relevant to byte-token attention in traffic models.

title: Parameterized Explainer for Graph Neural Network (PGExplainer)
authors: Dongsheng Luo et al.
relevance: Amortized, inductive GNN explainer generalizing across instances -- the second standard baseline in security-graph explanation evaluations (malware CFGs, NIDS flow graphs).

title: A Survey of Network-based Intrusion Detection Data Sets
authors: Markus Ring, Sarah Wunderlich, Deniz Scheuring, Dieter Landes, Andreas Hotho
relevance: The reference catalogue of 30+ NIDS datasets with 15 quality properties; its documented gaps (no perfect dataset, poor labeling, staleness) are the raw material every critique paper builds on.

title: Questioning the AI: Informing Design Practices for Explainable AI User Experiences
authors: Q. Vera Liao, Daniel Gruen, Sarah Miller
relevance: Interviews with 20 practitioners yielding the XAI Question Bank (what users actually ask of AI) -- a requirements-elicitation method transferable to asking what SOC analysts need from a traffic classifier's explanations.

title: From Anecdotal Evidence to Quantitative Evaluation Methods: A Systematic Review on Evaluating Explainable AI
authors: Meike Nauta, Jan Trienes et al.
relevance: The Co-12 properties (Correctness, Completeness, Consistency, Continuity, Compactness, ...) systematic review of 300+ papers; documents that a third of XAI papers evaluate only anecdotally.

title: Deep Fingerprinting: Undermining Website Fingerprinting Defenses with Deep Learning
authors: Payap Sirinam, Mohsen Imani, Marc Juarez, Matthew Wright
input_representation: packet direction sequence (+-1 vector, length 5000) of Tor traffic
relevance: Deep Fingerprinting: CNN over packet-direction sequences that broke WTF-PAD (98% on Tor); the sibling task (website fingerprinting) whose XAI treatments are frequently cross-cited by traffic-classification explanation work.

title: Deep Learning for Encrypted Traffic Classification: An Overview
authors: Shahbaz Rezaei, Xin Liu
input_representation: survey: taxonomy of raw bytes / time-series / header fields / flow statistics inputs
relevance: The standard early survey that fixed the taxonomy of input representations (raw bytes, packet time-series, header fields, flow statistics) and the general DL framework the XAI literature assumes.

title: E-GraphSAGE: A Graph Neural Network based Intrusion Detection System for IoT
authors: Wai Weng Lo et al.
relevance: The edge-feature GraphSAGE NIDS that most GNN-NIDS explainability papers (XG-BoT, TE-G-SAGE, X-CBA, E-GraphSAGE-with-explainability follow-ups) take as the model-under-explanation.

title: Evaluating XAI: A comparison of rule-based and example-based explanations
authors: Jasper van der Waa, Elisabeth Nieuwburg, Anita Cremers, Mark Neerincx
relevance: Careful user study: rule-based explanations modestly improve system understanding, but BOTH rule- and example-based explanations persuade users to follow wrong advice -- explanation as persuasion risk for analyst triage.

title: Anomal-E: A Self-Supervised Network Intrusion Detection System based on Graph Neural Networks
authors: Evan Caville et al.
relevance: Self-supervised edge-embedding GNN NIDS; the base system that X-CBA retrofits with explainability -- included as the second GNN hub for citation expansion.

title: Is Attention Explanation? An Introduction to the Debate
authors: Adrien Bibal et al.
relevance: Survey consolidating the attention-explanation debate across communities; notes 'the lack of communication is becoming more and more tangible' -- traffic/security is precisely such a disconnected community that reuses attention heatmaps uncritically.

title: Evolving cybersecurity frontiers: A comprehensive survey on concept drift and feature dynamics aware machine and deep learning in intrusion detection systems
authors: Methaq A. Shyaa, et al.
relevance: Main recent survey of drift-aware and feature-dynamics-aware ML/DL for IDS; useful map of detectors (ADWIN, Page-Hinkley, DDM) and adaptation strategies.

title: Navigating Shortcuts, Spurious Correlations, and Confounders: From Origins via Detection to Mitigation
authors: David Steinmann, Felix Divo, Maurice Kraus, Antonia Wuest, Lukas Struppek, et al.
relevance: Cross-domain survey unifying definitions, detection methods (including XAI-based detection) and mitigations for shortcut learning and spurious correlations - useful taxonomy for transferring shortcut-detection methodology into traffic classification.

title: DataZoo: Streamlining Traffic Classification Experiments
authors: Jan Luxemburk, Karel Hynek
relevance: Toolset standardizing dataset access, splits and metrics for traffic classification, created explicitly because ad-hoc dataset handling and undisclosed splits cause overly optimistic, irreproducible TC results.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Concept-Drift-Resilient Network Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Mateus Komarchesqui, V. G. D. S. Ruffo, Daniel Matheus Brandao Lent, et al.
relevance: Newest survey dedicated specifically to concept-drift-resilient NIDS, consolidating the 2021-2026 wave.

title: Attention and Representation Learning in Byte-Level Digital Forensics: A Survey of Methods, Challenges, and Applications
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications 17(2)
relevance: Survey of attention/representation learning over raw bytes (traffic and forensics) that explicitly lists interpretability, dataset bias, distribution shift and reproducibility as open challenges of byte-level attention models.

title: Does Explanation Correctness Matter? Linking Computational XAI Evaluation to Human Understanding
authors: Gregor Baer, Chao Zhang, Isel Grau, Pieter Van Gorp
relevance: N=200 study manipulating attribution correctness in time-series classification: correctness affects human understanding non-linearly and 'not all differences in functional correctness translate to differences in human understanding' -- links the benchmark world to the human world.

title: Neuro-Symbolic AI for Cybersecurity: State of the Art, Challenges, and Opportunities
authors: Safayat Bin Hakim, Muhammad Adil, Alvaro Velasquez, Shouhuai Xu, Houbing Herbert Song
relevance: Systematic review of 103 neural-symbolic security papers across IDS/malware/vulnerability discovery; useful hub for which NeSy formalisms (DeepProbLog, LTN, NLM) have and have not touched traffic data.

title: Network Intrusion Datasets: A Survey, Limitations, and Recommendations
relevance: Surveys the NIDS datasets on which all drift/generalization claims rest and catalogs their limitations (staleness, labeling errors, unrealistic traffic) - the data-side reason cross-dataset results collapse.

title: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Encrypted Traffic Classification on Resource-Constrained Devices
authors: Adel Chehade et al.
input_representation: 1D-CNN over raw bytes (ISCX VPN-nonVPN) under memory/compute constraints
relevance: HW-NAS compresses 1D-CNN raw-byte classifiers to IoT budgets on ISCX VPN-nonVPN; the tinyML end of the base-model spectrum where explanation cost also matters.

title: Unifying VXAI: A Systematic Review and Framework for the Evaluation of Explainable AI
relevance: 2025 systematic review unifying XAI evaluation into a structured framework of properties and metrics; a current map of the metric landscape.

title: What Makes for a Good Saliency Map? A User Study
authors: Leon Kares, Timo Speith, et al.
relevance: N=166 between-subjects comparison of LIME/Grad-CAM/Guided Backprop finding subjective and objective measures disagree and mathematical saliency metrics are often counterintuitive to humans.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Website Fingerprinting Attacks and Defenses in Tor: Advances and Open Challenges
authors: Yuwen Cui, et al.
relevance: Recent WF survey organizing datasets, attacks and defenses; explicitly contrasts interpretable traditional ML with higher-accuracy but opaque DL and lists multi-tab browsing and coarse-grained features as open challenges - useful framing source for the WF sub-angle.

title: A Systematic Review on the Integration of Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Intrusion Detection Systems to Enhancing Transparency and Interpretability in Cybersecurity
authors: (per Frontiers listing)
explanation_method: PRISMA systematic review of XAI-IDS
relevance: Most recent systematic review; useful for coverage checks and gap statements.

title: Comprehensive Survey on Adversarial Examples in Cybersecurity: Impacts, Challenges, and Mitigation Strategies
authors: (arXiv survey)
relevance: Broad survey of adversarial examples across cyber-security domains (malware, NIDS, spam), useful for situating traffic-classifier attacks in the wider threat landscape.

title: A Survey on Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Internet Traffic Classification and Prediction, and Intrusion Detection
authors: (survey)
relevance: Top-level survey of XAI methods across traffic classification, prediction, and intrusion detection -- the corpus-topic map into which this attack/robustness angle plugs.
_key: t:a survey on explainable artificial intelligence for internet traffic classification and prediction and intrusion detection

title: NetBench: A Large-Scale and Comprehensive Network Traffic Benchmark Dataset for Foundation Models
authors: Chen Qian et al.
input_representation: benchmark suite over packet/flow byte inputs, 20 tasks
relevance: Benchmark unifying 20 classification/generation tasks for traffic foundation models; the shared yardstick on which the 2024-2026 base models report.

title: Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection System for Industry 5.0: An Overview of the Literature, associated Challenges, the existing Solutions, and Potential Research Directions
authors: N. Moustafa et al. (per arXiv listing)
explanation_method: Survey of XAI-IDS incl. adversarial-XIDS
relevance: Recent survey cataloguing XAI-IDS solutions and open challenges for industrial deployments.

title: Logic Explained Networks
authors: Gabriele Ciravegna, Pietro Barbiero, Francesco Giannini, Marco Gori, Pietro Lio, Marco Maggini, Stefano Melacci
relevance: The LEN framework: neural models whose predictions come with learned First-Order Logic explanations -- a general self-explaining family whose only security use so far is malware (EMBER), never traffic classification.

title: Natural Example-Based Explainability: a Survey
authors: Antonin Poche, Lucas Hervier, Mohamed-Chafik Bakkay
relevance: Surveys example-based explanation forms (similar examples, counterfactual examples, prototypes, criticisms) -- the taxonomy for case-based explanation forms this angle would transplant to traffic.

title: In Search of Verifiability: Explanations Rarely Enable Complementary Performance in AI-Advised Decision Making
authors: Raymond Fok, Daniel S. Weld
relevance: Synthesis arguing explanations only help when they let the human VERIFY the answer, and most tasks don't afford verification -- predicts exactly when NIDS-alert explanations will and won't improve triage decisions.

title: Explainable Intrusion Detection Systems (X-IDS): A Survey of Current Methods, Challenges, and Opportunities
authors: Subash Neupane, Jesse Ables, William Anderson, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi, Ioana Banicescu, Maria Seale
relevance: Survey organizing X-IDS by white-box/black-box and by explanation mechanism, proposing an architecture for explainable IDS -- context hub from the same group that later built the eclectic rule-extraction IDS.

title: A Survey of Explainable Graph Neural Networks: Taxonomy and Evaluation Metrics
authors: Yiqiao Li et al.
relevance: Taxonomy and metrics (fidelity, sparsity, stability) for GNN explanations; supplies the evaluation vocabulary missing from most GNN-NIDS explainability papers.

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making
authors: Helena Vasconcelos, Matthew Jörke, Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Tobias Gerstenberg, Michael S. Bernstein, Ranjay Krishna
relevance: Five studies showing people strategically engage with explanations based on cost-benefit: explanations reduce overreliance when they cut verification effort enough -- a mechanism directly applicable to time-pressured alert triage.

title: Use-Case-Grounded Simulations for Explanation Evaluation (SimEvals)
authors: Valerie Chen, Nari Johnson, Nicholay Topin, Gregory Plumb, Ameet Talwalkar
relevance: Trains agents to screen which explanation methods are worth an expensive human study -- a practical answer to the cost of running SOC-analyst experiments.

title: Do Users Benefit From Interpretable Vision? A User Study, Baseline, And Dataset
authors: Leon Sixt, Martin Schuessler, Oana-Iuliana Popescu, Philipp Weiß, Tim Landgraf
relevance: N=240 study where a simple baseline (showing example outputs) beat concept-based explanations for bias discovery -- benchmark discipline for claims that sophisticated explanations help users.

title: Open-Source Framework for Encrypted Internet and Malicious Traffic Classification
authors: Ofek Bader, Adi Lichy, Amit Dvir, Ran Dubin, Chen Hajaj
relevance: An open-source unified pipeline (OSF-EIMTC) for encrypted/malicious traffic classification intended to make feature extraction and model evaluation reproducible across studies.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Cybersecurity: A Literature Survey
authors: F. Charmet, H. C. Tanuwidjaja, S. Ayoubi, P.-F. Gimenez, Y. Han, H. Jmila, G. Blanc, T. Takahashi, Z. Zhang
explanation_method: Survey covering XAI methods, applications to IDS/malware/phishing, and attacks against explanations
relevance: Broad cybersecurity-XAI survey with a dedicated IDS section and a taxonomy of adversarial attacks on explainers.

title: Neural Prototype Trees for Interpretable Fine-grained Image Recognition
authors: Meike Nauta, Ron van Bree, Christin Seifert
relevance: Combines prototypes with a globally interpretable tree structure (ProtoTree) -- a prototype+tree hybrid that would map naturally onto flow features but has never been tried there.

title: Jointly Attacking Graph Neural Network and its Explanations (GEAttack)
authors: Wenqi Fan et al.
relevance: Shows GNNExplainer/PGExplainer explanations can be adversarially manipulated together with predictions -- a robustness caveat that transfers directly to adversarial network-traffic settings.

title: CF-GNNExplainer: Counterfactual Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
authors: Ana Lucic et al.
relevance: Minimal edge-deletion counterfactuals for GNNs; the template for counterfactual explanation work now appearing in graph-based IDS (e.g. counterfactual GraphLIME defenses).

title: Manipulating and Measuring Model Interpretability
authors: Forough Poursabzi-Sangdeh, Daniel G. Goldstein, Jake M. Hofman, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan, Hanna Wallach
relevance: Pre-registered experiments (N=3,800): transparent models improved simulatability but did NOT improve reliance and actually hampered error detection via information overload -- the sharpest evidence that 'more transparency' can hurt the human.

title: Human-Centered Explainable AI (XAI): From Algorithms to User Experiences
authors: Q. Vera Liao, Kush R. Varshney
relevance: Survey bridging XAI algorithms and HCI evaluation practice; frames explainability as an inherently human-centric property to be validated with users, not benchmarks.

title: Explaining Machine Learning Classifiers through Diverse Counterfactual Explanations (DiCE)
authors: Ramaravind K. Mothilal, Amit Sharma, Chenhao Tan
relevance: Diversity- and feasibility-constrained counterfactual generation (DPP-based) for tabular models; DiCE is the standard library baseline the NIDS counterfactual papers (diffusion CF, CANDICE) compare against.

title: Concept Bottleneck Models
authors: Pang Wei Koh, Thao Nguyen, Yew Siang Tang, Stephen Mussmann, Emma Pierson, Been Kim, Percy Liang
relevance: Predict human concepts first, then the label, enabling test-time concept intervention; NO concept-bottleneck model for network traffic exists in any source searched -- the single clearest gap on this angle.

title: Why Attention is Not Explanation: Surgical Intervention and Causal Reasoning about Neural Models
authors: Christopher Grimsley, Elijah Mayfield, Julia R. S. Bursten
relevance: Argues from causal-inference grounds that attention-as-explanation fails because surgical interventions on attention are not well-defined causal manipulations; sharpens what 'validated as explanation' would even mean.
_key: t:why attention is not explanation surgical intervention and causal reasoning about neural models

title: Proxy Tasks and Subjective Measures Can Be Misleading in Evaluating Explainable AI Systems
authors: Zana Buçinca, Phoebe Lin, Krzysztof Z. Gajos, Elena L. Glassman
relevance: Shows proxy-task results and subjective trust/preference ratings do NOT predict real decision-making performance with explanations -- a methodological landmine for any 'analysts said they liked it' SOC-XAI evaluation.

title: Interpreting Interpretability: Understanding Data Scientists' Use of Interpretability Tools for Machine Learning
authors: Harmanpreet Kaur, Harsha Nori, Samuel Jenkins, Rich Caruana, Hanna Wallach, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan
relevance: Contextual inquiry (N=11) + survey (N=197): data scientists over-trust and misuse GAM/SHAP tooling and often cannot describe the visualizations -- practitioners misreading the very tools SOCs are told to adopt.

title: Explainable Machine Learning in Deployment
authors: Umang Bhatt, Alice Xiang, Shubham Sharma, Adrian Weller, Ankur Taly, Yunhan Jia, Joydeep Ghosh, Ruchir Puri, José M. F. Moura, Peter Eckersley
relevance: ~50 interviews across ~30 organizations: deployed explainability overwhelmingly serves ML engineers for debugging, not end users -- the deployment-reality check for claims that XAI serves analysts.

title: Effect of Confidence and Explanation on Accuracy and Trust Calibration in AI-Assisted Decision Making
authors: Yunfeng Zhang, Q. Vera Liao, Rachel K. E. Bellamy
relevance: Experiments showing confidence scores calibrate trust but 'trust calibration alone is not sufficient to improve AI-assisted decision making', and local explanations underdeliver -- relevant to confidence-vs-explanation design in alert UIs.

title: Evaluating Saliency Map Explanations for Convolutional Neural Networks: A User Study
authors: Ahmed Alqaraawi, Martin Schuessler, Philipp Weiß, Enrico Costanza, Nadia Berthouze
relevance: Between-subjects study: saliency maps gave 'very limited help' in predicting classifier behavior on new inputs -- cautionary for saliency-over-packet-bytes visualizations popular in DL traffic classification.

title: Actionable Recourse in Linear Classification
authors: Berk Ustun, Alexander Spangher, Yang Liu
relevance: Defines recourse (feasible, actionable feature changes via integer programming) -- the formal 'actionability' notion that NIDS counterfactual papers borrow informally; strict recourse auditing has NEVER been done for traffic classifiers.

title: This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition (ProtoPNet)
authors: Chaofan Chen, Oscar Li, Chaofan Tao, Alina Jade Barnett, Jonathan Su, Cynthia Rudin
relevance: Prototype-part case-based reasoning inside a deep net; its only traffic-side descendant is LEXNet (KDD 2023) -- no open-dataset ProtoPNet-for-flows replication exists.

title: Twin-Systems to Explain Artificial Neural Networks using Case-Based Reasoning: Comparative Tests of Feature-Weighting Methods in ANN-CBR Twins for XAI
authors: Eoin M. Kenny, Mark T. Keane
relevance: ANN-CBR twinning: map network feature weights into a case-based reasoner to produce explanation-by-example -- the systematic CBR-XAI method, untried on network traffic.

title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV)
authors: Been Kim, Martin Wattenberg, Justin Gilmer, Carrie Cai, James Wexler, Fernanda Viegas, Rory Sayres
relevance: Concept-based explanation via directional derivatives against user-defined concept vectors; in networking it has been tried exactly once (KDD'99, Robinson 2024) -- wide open for modern encrypted-traffic concepts.

title: Towards Robust Interpretability with Self-Explaining Neural Networks (SENN)
authors: David Alvarez-Melis, Tommi S. Jaakkola
relevance: Defines explicitness/faithfulness/stability criteria and builds models interpretable during learning -- the self-explaining-model manifesto; no SENN application to traffic was found.

title: Anchors: High-Precision Model-Agnostic Explanations
authors: Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Sameer Singh, Carlos Guestrin
relevance: IF-THEN rule ('anchor') local explanations with precision guarantees -- the rule-form local alternative to LIME/SHAP that IDS comparison studies occasionally include but rarely operationalize.
_key: t:anchors high precision model agnostic explanations

title: Deep k-Nearest Neighbors: Towards Confident, Interpretable and Robust Deep Learning
authors: Nicolas Papernot, Patrick McDaniel
relevance: Example-based (nearest training neighbors per layer) interpretability with adversarial-robustness motivation from security researchers -- case-based explanation machinery never ported to traffic classifiers.

title: Metrics for Explainable AI: Challenges and Prospects
authors: Robert R. Hoffman, Shane T. Mueller, Gary Klein, Jordan Litman
relevance: Measurement toolbox for human-grounded XAI evaluation: explanation goodness/satisfaction scales, comprehension tests, curiosity, appropriate trust/reliance, joint human-XAI performance.

title: Automated Website Fingerprinting through Deep Learning
authors: Vera Rimmer, Davy Preuveneers, Marc Juarez, Tom Van Goethem, Wouter Joosen
relevance: Shows DL automates WF feature engineering end-to-end, creating exactly the black-box (what did the network learn?) that later WF interpretability work (WeFDE-style leakage analysis, SHAP-driven attacks) responds to - task-defining hub.

title: Counterfactual Explanations Without Opening the Black Box: Automated Decisions and the GDPR
authors: Sandra Wachter, Brent Mittelstadt, Chris Russell
relevance: The founding counterfactual-explanation paper (minimal input change that flips the decision, no model internals needed) -- the conceptual root of every counterfactual NIDS explainer in this corpus.
_key: t:counterfactual explanations without opening the black box automated decisions and the gdpr

title: Distilling a Neural Network Into a Soft Decision Tree
authors: Nicholas Frosst, Geoffrey Hinton
relevance: Canonical soft-decision-tree distillation of DNNs -- the method family Trustee/Metis specialized for networking; useful methodological ancestor.

title: Explanation in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Social Sciences
authors: Tim Miller
relevance: Argues XAI is built on researcher intuition rather than what philosophy/psychology know about how people actually give and take explanations (contrastive, selected, social) -- the standard critique cited when explanations fail users.
